summary: Target-level plan of Direct summands and big Cohen–Macaulay algebras. DS.0 defines split algebras, splinters, big and balanced big Cohen–Macaulay modules and the splitting obstruction, proves that completion balances big Cohen–Macaulay modules and that balanced ones are faithfully flat over regular local rings, reduces the splitting problem to complete local domains with a discriminant, and settles the characteristic-zero (trace) and low-dimensional cases. DS.1 proves Hochster's endomorphism criterion and the corrected pure-to-split theorem over complete local rings, and the characteristic-p direct summand theorem. DS.2 is André's proof for W(k)⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧ through splitting modulo p^m. DS.3 is Bhatt's proof for complete regular local rings through perfectoid covers, obstruction detection, almost splitting on annuli and the quantitative Riemann extension theorem. DS.4 constructs balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras through almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras and Hochster's partial algebra modifications (André in mixed characteristic, Hochster–Huneke in equal characteristic) and weak functoriality from almost Cohen–Macaulay squares. DS.5 states the direct summand theorem once with both routes, flat domination of finite covers, the splitting of R → R⁺ and the monomial theorem. DS.6 proves that pure subrings of regular local rings of mixed characteristic are Cohen–Macaulay. DS.7 is Bhatt's derived direct summand theorem. Purity, almost purity, the Abhyankar lemma, Kummer towers and the Riemann extension theorems are imported from PerfectoidSpacesPartII.

nodes.title: Split algebras (R-linear retractions of the unit)
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and S a commutative R-algebra with structure map ι : R → S. A splitting of S over R is an R-linear map ρ : S → R with ρ ∘ ι = id_R, equivalently ρ(1) = 1. S is split over R (ι splits) if a splitting exists. No multiplicativity of ρ is required. Writing ev : Hom_R(S, R) → R for evaluation at 1, S is split iff ev is surjective, and the image of ev is an ideal of R (the trace ideal of 1).
hypotheses: Splittings are R-module maps, never ring maps: ℝ → ℂ is split by the real part, which is not multiplicative.

When S is a finitely presented R-module, splitting is equivalent to purity of ι (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map; in the proof of André B Lemme A.2.1(4) Hom_S(S, R) is read as Hom_R(S, R), misprint DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E19).
proofSteps: The image of ev is an ideal: for f ∈ Hom_R(S, R) and r ∈ R, (r·f)(1) = r·f(1). If ev(f) = u is a unit, u⁻¹f is a splitting.
Composition: splittings of R → S and S → T (the latter S-linear) compose to an R-linear splitting of R → T; if R → S → T splits then the restriction of a splitting of R → T to S splits R → S.
Base change: if ρ splits ι then R′ ⊗_R ρ splits R′ → R′ ⊗_R S for every R-algebra R′.

Finite case: if R is Noetherian and S is a finite R-module, S is finitely presented, so Hom_R(S, R) is finite and its formation commutes with flat base change; hence the ideal ev(Hom_R(S, R)) commutes with flat base change, so splitting can be checked after localising at every maximal ideal, and descends along any faithfully flat R → R′ (an ideal I with IR′ = R′ is R).
acceptance: For K a field, K → L splits for every nonzero K-algebra L (extend 1 to a basis).

For R = K[x, y]/(xy) and its normalisation S = K[x] × K[y], R → S is finite and injective but not split (André B §0.2): its splitting would make R → S pure, but the ideal (x + y) of R is not contracted from S.

nodes.title: Splinters
nodes.statement: A commutative ring R is a splinter if it is Noetherian and reduced, and every finite injective ring map R → S (S commutative) is split in the sense of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra. Equivalently (R Noetherian and reduced) every integral injective ring map R → S is pure (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map), since an integral extension is the filtered union of its finite subalgebras.
hypotheses: The convention follows Bhatt–Ma–Patakfalvi–Schwede–Tucker–Waldron–Witaszek, Definition 2.12. Bhatt [Bhatt12] Definition 0.1 instead asks splitting of O_S → f_*O_X for every finite surjective f : X → Spec S; for Noetherian rings the two agree once R is reduced, and the scheme version forces reducedness (apply it to R_red → R).
Reducedness is part of the definition: without it the Artinian Gorenstein ring k[ε]/(ε²), which is self-injective, would satisfy the splitting condition.
proofSteps: Integral version: an integral extension R ⊆ S is the filtered union of finite subalgebras S_α; each R → S_α splits hence is pure, and pure maps are stable under filtered colimits (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map).
Contracted ideals: for a pure extension R → S and every ideal I of R, R/I → S/IS is injective, so IS ∩ R = I.

A splinter domain is integrally closed: if a/b ∈ Frac(R) is integral over R, then R → R[a/b] is finite and injective; a splitting gives R[a/b] ≅ R ⊕ R[a/b]/R, so the quotient, which is killed by powers of b, is also torsion-free as a submodule of Frac(R), hence zero, and a/b ∈ R (Bhatt [Bhatt12] Example 1.1).
acceptance: Every field is a splinter.
A Noetherian domain containing ℚ is a splinter iff it is normal (Bhatt [Bhatt12] Example 1.1; DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/trace-retraction).

Defines splinters through finite surjective maps of schemes and shows that a connected Noetherian ℚ-scheme is a splinter iff it is normal.
The direct summand conjecture says that every Noetherian regular ring is a splinter in this sense.

nodes.title: Big Cohen–Macaulay modules and algebras
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring of Krull dimension d and x = (x_1, …, x_d) a system of parameters of R (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/systems-of-parameters, applied to M = R). An R-module M, not necessarily finitely generated, is big Cohen–Macaulay for x if M ≠ mM and x is weakly regular on M: for each 0 ≤ i < d, x_{i+1} is a nonzerodivisor on M/(x_1, …, x_i)M. M is big Cohen–Macaulay if it is big Cohen–Macaulay for some system of parameters. An R-algebra C is a big Cohen–Macaulay algebra (for x) if it is so as an R-module.
hypotheses: Because (x) is m-primary, M ≠ mM is equivalent to M ≠ (x)M; so for a system of parameters the condition is exactly Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M x.
No finiteness is imposed on M; for finitely generated M the notion is that of a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module.
In dimension 0 the empty sequence is the system of parameters and every module with M ≠ mM qualifies.
proofSteps: The equivalence M ≠ mM ⟺ M ≠ (x)M: m^n ⊆ (x) for some n, so M = mM gives M = m^n M ⊆ (x)M.
Hence big Cohen–Macaulay for x is RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M x with x a system of parameters, and the Mathlib API for regular sequences applies.
acceptance: A regular local ring is big Cohen–Macaulay over itself for a regular system of parameters.

sources.match: Calls a not necessarily Noetherian B-algebra C Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x) when C ≠ m_B C and the system of parameters x becomes a regular sequence in C.

nodes.title: Balanced big Cohen–Macaulay modules and algebras
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring. An R-module M is balanced big Cohen–Macaulay if M ≠ mM and every system of parameters of R is weakly regular on M, i.e. M is big Cohen–Macaulay (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/big-cm-module) for every system of parameters. An R-algebra C is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra if it is so as an R-module; André calls these Cohen–Macaulay B-algebras.
hypotheses: For finitely generated nonzero M, balanced and big agree. For arbitrary modules they can differ; m-adic completion passes from big to balanced (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/completion-balances), with the arbitrary-module completion input recorded in G3.
proofSteps: Unfold: balanced means IsBigCohenMacaulayFor x M for all systems of parameters x.
Change of rings: a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for B is one for any local subring A ⊆ B over which B is finite with the same systems of parameters (used in André B Remarque 4.2.1).
acceptance: Over a regular local ring a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra is faithfully flat (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/regular-big-cm-flat).

sources.match: A B-algebra is Cohen–Macaulay if it is Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x) for every system of parameters x; the footnote identifies this with balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras.

nodes.title: Completion turns big Cohen–Macaulay modules into balanced ones
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local ring and M an R-module with M ≠ mM on which some system of parameters x of R is weakly regular. Then the m-adic completion M̂ = lim_n M/m^n M is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay R-module (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/balanced-big-cm-module). If M is an R-algebra, M̂ is an R-algebra and M → M̂ is an algebra map.
hypotheses: M̂ is the adic completion of M as an R-module (Mathlib AdicCompletion); M itself need not be separated.
The source states the arbitrary-module theorem, but its proof and the Ext/Čech comparison remain G3; the Bruns–Herzog book cited there was not independently read.
proofSteps: A system of parameters weakly regular on M implies H^i_m(M) = 0 for i < d by the direct limit of the Koszul complexes on its powers. This needs the Čech/Koszul comparison with Mathlib’s Ext-colimit localCohomology; the baseline definition alone does not provide that comparison.

Apply the arbitrary-module completion/change-of-parameters theorem recalled in André §4.1, p. 85, and BMPSTWW §2.2, p. 12: this vanishing together with M/mM ≠ 0 makes the m-adic completion balanced. G3 records this non-routine input; it does not follow from the finite-module depth criterion or from merely defining a Koszul complex.
Completion is functorial, and for an algebra the inverse limit of the quotient algebras carries the required algebra structure. No finite-generation or separatedness assumption on M is inserted.
acceptance: For M finitely generated, M̂ = M ⊗_R R̂ and the statement reduces to the classical fact that a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module stays maximal Cohen–Macaulay after completion.

sources.match: One passes from Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x) to Cohen–Macaulay for every system of parameters by m_B-adic completion, citing Bartijn–Strooker Théorème 1.7.
If M satisfies the local cohomology vanishing (a) and M/mM ≠ 0, then the m-adic completion satisfies (c), citing Bruns–Herzog Exercise 8.1.7 and Theorem 8.5.1.
Uses the same completion step (Bruns–Herzog Corollary 8.5.3) to make the modification algebras balanced.

nodes.title: Balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras over regular local rings are faithfully flat
nodes.statement: Let A be a Noetherian regular local ring and C a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay A-module (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/balanced-big-cm-module). Then C is faithfully flat over A. In particular a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay A-algebra is a faithfully flat A-algebra.
hypotheses: Use the corrected exact Tor segment in E18 and choose the maximal regular sequence by ht P, not by the descending Tor degree i; these are independent indices.
proofSteps: Every finitely generated A-module M has projective dimension at most n + 1 = dim A (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/regular-local-finite-pd), so Tor^A_i(M, C) = 0 for i > dim A.

For the descending induction on the Tor degree i > 0, reduce by a prime filtration to M = A/P. Choose a maximal A-regular sequence x_1,…,x_h in P, of length h = ht P, independently of i; it extends to a system of parameters. For N = A/(x_1,…,x_h), the prime P is associated to N: N is Cohen–Macaulay and its localisation at P has dimension zero. Thus A/P embeds in N. The Koszul resolution of N and weak regularity on C give Tor_j(N,C)=0 for all j>0.
The exact segment Tor_{i+1}(N/M, C) → Tor_i(M, C) → Tor_i(N, C) has vanishing outer terms (the first by the induction hypothesis), so Tor_i(M, C) = 0: C is flat.
mC ≠ C gives faithful flatness for the local ring A (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat).
acceptance: For A = C a regular local ring the statement is trivial; for A a DVR it says a torsion-free module with C ≠ ϖC is faithfully flat.

sources.match: Every Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra is Cohen–Macaulay over the regular subring A and hence faithfully flat over A; the footnote proves flatness by descending induction on Tor using finite projective dimension and prime filtrations.
Over a regular ring an algebra is Cohen–Macaulay iff it is faithfully flat.

nodes.title: The splitting obstruction of a unit map
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and u : A → K a morphism in the derived category D(A) (Mathlib DerivedCategory of A-modules), for example the unit A → B of a finite A-algebra or A → RΓ(X, O_X) for an A-scheme X. Complete it to a distinguished triangle A → K → Q_u → A[1] and let α_u ∈ Hom_{D(A)}(Q_u, A[1]) be the connecting morphism. Then u has a left inverse in D(A) iff α_u = 0 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/splitting-through-comparison). For a finite injective algebra A → B, Q_u = B/A in degree 0 and α_u is the class of the extension 0 → A → B → B/A → 0 in Ext¹_A(B/A, A); it vanishes iff B is split over A (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra).
hypotheses: α_u depends on the triangle only up to automorphisms of Q_u fixing the triangle; its vanishing does not.

For A → A′ any ring map the derived base change carries α_u to α_{u′} for u′ = u ⊗^L_A A′; vanishing of α_{u′} implies vanishing of α_u only when the base change map on Hom groups is injective, for example for A → A′ faithfully flat and Q_u pseudo-coherent with A Noetherian.
proofSteps: Existence and characterisation of α_u: the triangle obstruction lemma EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/splitting-through-comparison.

Flat base change: if Q_u is pseudo-coherent (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7/pseudo-coherent-object) and A → A′ is flat, Hom_{D(A)}(Q_u, A[1]) ⊗_A A′ ≅ Hom_{D(A′)}(Q_u ⊗^L A′, A′[1]) (Stacks 0A6A), compatibly with α.

For A Noetherian and I-adically complete, represent pseudo-coherent Q_u by a bounded-above complex of finite free modules. In each fixed cohomological degree its dual uses only finitely many adjacent finite modules. Artin–Rees exactness of I-adic quotient pro-systems gives {H^j RHom(Q_u,A)/I^m}_m ≅ {H^j RHom(Q_u,A/I^m)}_m as pro-systems, with lim¹ zero. Taking j=1 gives the required Hom inverse limit. This is a degreewise argument extending the finite-module supplier; no uniform assertion for unbounded complexes is needed.
acceptance: For a nonzero finite free A-algebra B, the element 1 is primitive at every maximal ideal (Nakayama applied to B); therefore B/A is finite locally free, hence projective, and Ext¹_A(B/A,A)=0. In the concrete case ℤ → ℤ[i], the quotient is free of rank one. Global freeness of B/A is not required.

sources.match: Introduces the boundary map α_0 ∈ Hom_{A_0}(Q_0, A_0[1]) of the triangle A_0 → B_0 → Q_0 as the obstruction to splitting, and reduces its vanishing to vanishing modulo p^m using p-adic completeness and Lemma 5.3.
Uses the class e of the extension 0 → Ā → B̄ → B̄/Ā → 0 modulo p^m and shows it vanishes.

nodes.title: Reductions of the splitting problem
nodes.statement: Let A_0 → B_0 be a finite injective ring map with A_0 Noetherian regular. For every maximal ideal m of A_0 and every field extension K of A_0/m there is a complete Noetherian regular local ring A, faithfully flat over (A_0)_m, with m A = m_A and residue field K; and B = B_0 ⊗_{A_0} A has a prime 𝔮 with 𝔮 ∩ A = 0. A_0 → B_0 splits (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra) as soon as, for every m, the finite injective map A → B/𝔮 splits for one such A and one such 𝔮. If A has mixed characteristic (0, p), then B/𝔮 is a domain finite over the normal domain A and there is g ∈ A, outside every minimal prime of pA (so g ≠ 0 in A/p), such that B/𝔮[1/(pg)] is finite étale over A[1/(pg)].
hypotheses: The completion is taken before passing to the domain quotient: completion need not preserve the domain property (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E10, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E14).
The domain reduction is needed before choosing g (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E9, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E9).
proofSteps: Localise: splitting of a finite algebra over a Noetherian ring is checked at maximal ideals (API Algebra.IsSplit.of_localization_maximal).

Complete and extend the residue field: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/completed-residue-extension-exists gives a complete Noetherian local A faithfully flat over (A_0)_m with m A = m_A and residue field K; A is regular because m_A is generated by dim A elements. Splitting descends along faithfully flat maps (Algebra.IsSplit.of_faithfullyFlat_baseChange).

Domain quotient: A → B is injective and integral, so some prime 𝔮 of B lies over 0 (lying over for the minimal prime 0 of the domain A, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/regular-local-domain); a splitting of A → B/𝔮 composed with B → B/𝔮 splits A → B.

Discriminant: B/𝔮 is a domain finite over the normal domain A of characteristic 0, so Frac(B/𝔮)/Frac(A) is finite separable and A → B/𝔮 is generically étale (Mathlib Algebra.Etale). The non-étale locus in Spec A[1/p] has closure Z of codimension ≥ 1 whose codimension-one components are height-one primes not containing p; a minimal prime P of pA has height one and contains p, so P ∉ Z, and prime avoidance gives g in the ideal of Z outside every minimal prime of pA.
acceptance: The reductions preserve the conclusion in all three characteristic types: equal characteristic 0, equal characteristic p and mixed characteristic (0, p).

nodes.title: Trace splittings and the characteristic-zero direct summand theorem
nodes.statement: Let R be a Noetherian integrally closed domain and S a domain containing R and finite over R, with d = [Frac(S) : Frac(R)]. If d is a unit in R, then d⁻¹·Tr_{Frac(S)/Frac(R)} restricts to an R-linear splitting S → R. Consequently every Noetherian normal domain containing ℚ is a splinter, and every Noetherian regular ring containing ℚ is a splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splinter).
hypotheses: The characteristic-zero statement uses the domain reduction of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions (a regular local ring is a normal domain) and the fact that a splitting of A → B/𝔮 splits A → B.
Bhatt says 'characteristic 0' for this case; the trace argument needs ℚ ⊆ R (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E8, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E3).
proofSteps: For s ∈ S the trace Tr(s) is integral over R (sum of conjugates of an integral element) and lies in Frac(R), hence in R by normality (Mathlib Algebra.trace, IsIntegrallyClosed).
Tr(1) = d (Mathlib Algebra.trace_algebraMap), so d⁻¹Tr is a splitting.
For a general finite injective R → S with R a normal domain containing ℚ, choose a prime 𝔮 of S over 0; the trace splitting of R → S/𝔮 splits R → S.
acceptance: Invertibility of d matters for the trace construction: for ℤ → ℤ[(1 + √5)/2], d = 2 and d⁻¹Tr((1 + √5)/2) = 1/2 ∉ ℤ, so d⁻¹Tr is not a ℤ-linear map to ℤ, although the extension (being free) still splits by the coefficient of 1.

sources.match: When the degree of the extension is invertible, a divided trace gives a retraction, which proves the conjecture when R contains ℚ.
For a normal Noetherian ℚ-scheme, (1/d)·Tr gives a canonical splitting of O_S → f_*O_X for finite surjective f, using that the trace preserves integrality.

nodes.title: The direct summand theorem in dimension at most two
nodes.statement: Let A be a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension at most 2 and A → S a finite injective ring map. Then A → S splits. More precisely, for a domain S finite over A containing A, the reflexive hull S** = Hom_A(Hom_A(S, A), A) is a finite free A-algebra containing S, so A → S** splits and hence A → S splits.
hypotheses: Any characteristic. The statement is the case André B §0.2 calls easy: finite flat extensions split, and in dimension ≤ 2 normal (reflexive) finite extensions are flat.
proofSteps: Reduce to S a domain containing A (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions, the domain step).
S** is the intersection of the localisations S_𝔭 over height-one primes 𝔭 of A inside S ⊗ Frac(A), hence a ring containing S, and it is a finitely generated reflexive A-module.

A reflexive module over a regular local ring of dimension ≤ 2 has depth min(2, dim A) = dim A, so by Auslander–Buchsbaum (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/auslander-buchsbaum) it is free; a finite free A-algebra containing A splits (1 extends to a basis after reducing modulo m_A, since 1 ∉ m_A S**).
acceptance: In dimension 1 (A a DVR) every torsion-free finite A-module is free, so every finite extension domain splits.
For dimension 3 in mixed characteristic the statement is Heitmann's theorem (André B §0.2), here a special case of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/direct-summand-theorem.

sources.match: The conjecture is easy for finite flat extensions, which then split, and this settles dimension ≤ 2 because every finite normal extension of R is flat there; dimension 3 is Heitmann's theorem.
When dim A_0 ≤ 2 the theorem follows from the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula.

nodes.title: Hochster's endomorphism criterion for splitting
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a nonzero local ring, not necessarily Noetherian, and r ∈ m such that ∩_{n≥1} r^n R = 0 and either r = 0 or r is a nonzerodivisor on R. Let σ : R → R be a local ring endomorphism such that R is a free module over σ(R) and ∩_{j≥0} σ^j(m)R ⊆ rR. Let R ⊆ S be a ring extension and τ : S → S an injective ring endomorphism restricting to σ on R. If Hom_R(S, R) ≠ 0, then R → S splits (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra).
hypotheses: The hypothesis 'r = 0 or r a nonzerodivisor' is added to André's statement, which only asks R to be r-adically separated: dividing a functional by a power of r needs it (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E2, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E4).
The linear form in the proof is defined on the finite free summand M, not on N (misprint DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E1, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E2).
proofSteps: Take λ ∈ Hom_R(S, R) nonzero. Since ∩ r^nR = 0 and r is regular (or zero), divide λ by the largest power of r dividing all its values, then precompose with multiplication by some s ∈ S, to get λ(1) ∉ rR.
Then λ(1) ∉ σ^j(m)R for some j, by the hypothesis on ∩σ^j(m)R.

R is free over σ^j(R), a local ring with maximal ideal σ^j(m); choose a finite free σ^j(R)-summand M of R with λ(1) ∈ M ∖ σ^j(m)M and, by Nakayama, a σ^j(R)-linear form μ on M with μ(λ(1)) = 1, extended by 0 on a complement.
μ ∘ λ restricted to τ^j(S) is a σ^j(R)-linear retraction of σ^j(R) → τ^j(S); transporting along the isomorphisms σ^j : R → σ^j(R) and τ^j : S → τ^j(S) gives an R-linear retraction of R → S.
acceptance: With r = 0 and σ = Frobenius this is the characteristic-p splitting criterion (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.1/frobenius-direct-summand).

With R = V⟦x_2, …, x_d⟧ for a complete DVR V with uniformiser r and σ(x_i) = x_i^q (q ≥ 2), R is free over σ(R) with monomial basis of exponents < q and ∩σ^j(m)R = rR; this is the case used for R → R⁺ (Hochster 1983 6.1, André A.3 Applications).

sources.locator: Annexe A.3, Proposition A.3.1, implication (c) ⇒ (b) and its proof, pp. 90–91
sources.match: For a local ring R, r-adically separated, with a local endomorphism σ making R free over σ(R) and ∩σ^m(m)R ⊆ rR, and an extension S on which σ extends injectively, a nonzero element of Hom_R(S, R) yields an R-linear retraction, by producing a retraction of σ^m(R) → σ^m(S) and transporting it.

sources.locator: §1, Theorem 2, statement p. 31 and first characteristic-p proof p. 32
sources.match: Historical special case: for a module-finite domain extension of a complete regular local ring of characteristic p, a nonzero dual functional and iterated Frobenius contradict a bad monomial relation. The abstract endomorphism criterion here is André Proposition A.3.1, not a theorem stated on Hochster p. 30.

nodes.title: Pure maps out of complete local rings split
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a complete Noetherian local ring and S a commutative R-algebra such that R → S is pure (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map). Then R → S splits (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra). No finiteness, integrality or endomorphism of S is needed.
hypotheses: Completeness is essential: Datta–Murayama Proposition 5.4.1(iii) gives an excellent Henselian DVR V of characteristic p with Hom_V(V^{1/p}, V) = 0, so V → V^{1/p} is faithfully flat, hence pure, but not split. This corrects André B Proposition A.3.1, implication (a) ⇒ (b) for regular R and integral S, and its application to V⟦T⟧ → V⟦T⟧⁺ for an arbitrary DVR V (source issues DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E3 and E4, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E5 and E21).
proofSteps: Let E be the injective hull of the residue field (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/residue-injective-hull). Purity makes E = E ⊗_R R → E ⊗_R S injective.
E is injective, so restriction Hom_R(E ⊗_R S, E) → Hom_R(E, E) is surjective.

Hom_R(E, E) = R̂ = R for complete R (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/matlis-duality), and by adjunction Hom_R(E ⊗_R S, E) = Hom_R(S, Hom_R(E, E)) = Hom_R(S, R); under these identifications the restriction map is evaluation at 1.
Hence evaluation at 1 on Hom_R(S, R) is surjective and R → S splits.
acceptance: R = K a field: every nonzero K-algebra splits.
The Datta–Murayama DVR is a non-example showing that 'complete' cannot be replaced by 'excellent Henselian'.

sources.locator: Annexe A.3, Proposition A.3.1, implication (a) ⇒ (c) and its proof, p. 91

nodes.title: The direct summand theorem in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian regular ring of characteristic p > 0 is a splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splinter).
hypotheses: The proof uses the reductions of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions with a perfect residue field.
proofSteps: By DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions it suffices to split A → S for A a complete regular local ring of characteristic p with perfect residue field k and S a domain finite over A.

A ≅ k⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧ (coefficient field DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/equal-characteristic-section and Cohen's presentation DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/cohen-series-presentation, the kernel being 0 by regularity), so Frobenius F : A → A is finite and A is free over F(A) = A^p with monomial basis (Kunz, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/kunz-and-henselian-f-finite).
Hom_A(S, A) ≠ 0: S is a finite torsion-free A-module, so S ⊗ Frac(A) ≅ Frac(A)^n and a nonzero Frac(A)-linear form, scaled by a common denominator of its values on generators, maps S to A.
Apply DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.1/endomorphism-retraction-criterion with r = 0, σ = F on A and τ = F on S (injective since S is reduced).
acceptance: For A = 𝔽_p⟦x⟧ and S = A[x^{1/p}] = 𝔽_p⟦x^{1/p}⟧, the splitting is the coefficient projection onto the monomials with integer exponent.

nodes.title: Splittings modulo powers of an ideal give a splitting
nodes.statement: Let A be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of A, and S a finite A-algebra. If for every m ≥ 1 the map A/I^m → S/I^m S splits (as A/I^m-modules), then A → S splits (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra).
hypotheses: André passes through the Artinian quotients A/(p^m, T_1^{p^m}, …, T_n^{p^m}) and Hochster's coset-stabilisation argument (Hochster 1973 p. 30); the Artin–Rees pro-isomorphism used here (Bhatt Lemma 5.3) needs only the powers of one ideal in the Jacobson radical.
proofSteps: By DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/adic-hom-pro-comparison the towers {Hom_A(S, A)/I^n} and {Hom_A(S, A/I^n)} are pro-isomorphic; in particular for each n there is m ≥ n such that the image of Hom_A(S, A/I^m) in Hom_A(S, A/I^n) lies in the image of Hom_A(S, A).
A splitting of A/I^m → S/I^mS is an element φ_m ∈ Hom_A(S, A/I^m) with φ_m(1) = 1. Its image in Hom_A(S, A/I^n) lifts to f ∈ Hom_A(S, A) with f(1) ≡ 1 modulo I^n.
f(1) ∈ 1 + I is a unit since I lies in the Jacobson radical, so f(1)⁻¹f is a splitting.
acceptance: For A a complete local ring and I = m_A this reproves that splitting of a finite algebra can be checked on Artinian quotients.

nodes.title: Splitting modulo p^m of finite extensions of W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, A = W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧, and B a domain containing A and finite over A, with g ∈ A ∖ pA such that B[1/(pg)] is finite étale over A[1/(pg)]. Then for every m ≥ 1 the map A/p^m → B/p^mB is injective and admits an A/p^m-linear retraction.
hypotheses: The setup (B a domain, g outside pA, étale after inverting pg) is supplied by DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions for unramified A, where pA is prime.
proofSteps: Injectivity: A is integrally closed in A[1/p] and A → B is injective and integral, so p^mB ∩ A = p^mA.

Let S = (Â°_∞∞)_{!!} be the faithfully flat A-algebra of PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/flat-integral-model; S/p^m is flat over A/p^m and B/p^m is finitely presented over A/p^m, so Ext¹_{A/p^m}(B̄/Ā, Ā) ⊗ S/p^m ≅ Ext¹_{S/p^m}((B̄ ⊗ S/p^m)/(S/p^m), S/p^m) (flat base change of Ext for finitely presented modules over a Noetherian ring, DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splitting-obstruction).

By PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/ramified-kummer-almost-flatness (André B Corollaire 3.2.2), S/p^m → (B ⊗_A S)/p^m is almost pure in the setup (K°_∞ + K°°_∞[T^{1/p^∞}], T^{1/p^∞}K°°_∞[T^{1/p^∞}]) with T^{1/p^h} acting as g^{1/p^h}; by PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/almost-pure-map (Lemme A.4.1) the class e ⊗ 1 of the base-changed extension is killed by g^{1/p^∞}K°°_∞.

Apply PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/krull-detection-lemma with R = A/p^m, M = R·e, S/p^m faithfully flat and K = g^{1/p^∞}K°°_∞ S/p^m (idempotent): K kills M ⊗ S/p^m and K ∩ R contains the class of pg, which is nonzero for m ≥ 2. Hence M = 0, i.e. e = 0, and A/p^m → B/p^m splits; m = 1 follows from m = 2.
acceptance: When B[1/p] is already étale over A[1/p] (g = 1) the argument only needs Faltings' almost purity; this is the case proved earlier by Bhatt and Shimomoto (André B §0.4).

sources.match: A/p^m → B/p^m is injective because A is integrally closed in A[1/p]; the algebra (Â°_∞∞)_{!!} is faithfully flat over A, equal to A°_∞0 + K°°_∞Â°_∞∞ and stable under multiplication by (ϖg)^{1/p^∞}.
The fragment of the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma used: almost faithful flatness of Â°_∞∞/p^m → B°/p^m, and almost purity of (Â°_∞∞)_{!!}/p^m → (B ⊗ (Â°_∞∞)_{!!})/p^m.

nodes.title: André's direct summand theorem for W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p. Then A = W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧ is a splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splinter): every finite injective A-algebra B splits over A.
hypotheses: The theorem is André B Théorème 0.2.1. André deduces the general regular case from it through Hochster's reduction (Hochster 1983 Theorem 6.1); this roadmap reaches the general case instead through DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/direct-summand-theorem, by Bhatt's theorem or by flat domination, so Hochster's 1983 reduction is not a target.
proofSteps: Reduce to B a domain with a discriminant g ∈ A ∖ pA (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions; A is local, complete, with perfect residue field, and pA is prime).
A/p^m → B/p^mB splits for every m (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.2/mod-p-power-splitting).
Apply DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.2/adic-splitting-criterion with I = pA, which lies in the maximal ideal of the local ring A.
acceptance: For Kummer extensions B = integral closure of A in A[g^{1/p^k}][1/p] the splitting also follows from purity of Kummer extensions without the Abhyankar fragment (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/kummer-purity, André B Corollaire 2.6.1).
André also notes that W(k)⟦T⟧ → W(k)⟦T⟧⁺ splits; this is DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/absolute-integral-closure-splits.

sources.match: The direct summand conjecture holds for W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧, hence (with Hochster's reduction) for every regular ring.
Proof: reduction to a domain with a discriminant g, splitting modulo every p^m, and passage to the limit.
Purity of Kummer extensions gives the Kummer case without the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma.

nodes.title: Cohen presentations of complete regular local rings of mixed characteristic
nodes.statement: Let (A_0, m, k) be a complete Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) and dimension d, with k perfect, and fix a continuous local coefficient map ι : W(k) → A_0 inducing the identity of k (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/cohen-coefficient-map). All presentations are W(k)-algebra maps for this ι. (1) Unramified case p ∉ m²: A_0 ≅ W(k)⟦x_2, …, x_d⟧. (2) Ramified case p ∈ m²: for any generators x_1, …, x_d of m, the surjection ψ : W(k)⟦X_1, …, X_d⟧ → A_0, X_i ↦ x_i, has kernel generated by one element p − f with f ∈ (p, X_1, …, X_d)², f having no constant term and p ∤ f.
hypotheses: Only this regular-local corollary is planned here; the coefficient ring and its presentations are DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1's.
proofSteps: (1) p is part of a regular system of parameters (p, x_2, …, x_d); the map W(k)⟦X_2, …, X_d⟧ → A_0 is surjective (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/cohen-series-presentation) between regular local rings of the same dimension, hence an isomorphism (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/regular-surjection-kernel).

(2) ψ is a surjection of regular local rings of dimensions d + 1 and d, so its kernel is generated by one element h that is part of a regular system of parameters (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/regular-surjection-kernel). Since p ∈ m² is in the image of (p, X)², p ≡ f′ modulo ker ψ for some f′ ∈ (p, X)², and h can be taken as p − f with f ∈ (p, X)².

Write the initial generator as p − f_0 with f_0 ∈ (p,X)² and constant term c ∈ p²W(k). Put u = 1 − c/p, a unit of W(k), and f = (f_0 − c)/u. Multiplying the generator by u⁻¹ gives p − f; now f has zero constant term and is still in (p,X)². If p divides f then p − f is p times a unit, forcing characteristic p, contrary to mixed characteristic.
acceptance: A_0 = ℤ_p[√p]⟦x_2⟧ ≅ ℤ_p⟦X_1, X_2⟧/(p − X_1²) is a ramified example with f = X_1².

sources.match: In the unramified case A_0 ≅ W⟦x_2, …, x_d⟧; in the ramified case a surjection from W⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧ has kernel generated by p − f with f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_d)² a power series without constant term and not divisible by p.

nodes.title: Perfectoid covers of regular local rings
nodes.statement: Let A_0 be a p-torsion-free Noetherian regular local ring with residue characteristic p, and K = Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^ with t = p. After replacing A_0 by a complete regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field k that is faithfully flat over it, construct A_0 → A as follows. Unramified case (A_0 ≅ W(k)⟦x_2, …, x_d⟧): A is the p-adic completion of A_0[p^{1/p^∞}, x_2^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]. Ramified case (A_0 = W(k)⟦X_1, …, X_d⟧/(p − f)): let P_m = W(k)⟦X^{1/p^m}⟧ and A′ the p-adic completion of colim_m P_m/(p − f); there is a unit u ∈ A′ with g^p = pu, where g = σ^{-1}(f)(X^{1/p}) ∈ P_1 (σ the Witt vector Frobenius), so A′[1/p] is a perfectoid Tate ring with a pseudouniformizer π, π^p = pv for a unit v; let A be the π-adic completion of the integral closure of A′ in A′[1/p][v^{1/p^∞}], normalised by passing to almost elements. In both cases A is an integral perfectoid K°-algebra in which p has a compatible system of p-power roots.
hypotheses: The field normalisation of the ramified case adjoins roots of v to A′[1/p] and takes the integral closure; the roots of p lie in the new algebra A, not in A′ (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E5, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E2).
A is an integral perfectoid K°-algebra, not a K-algebra (misprint DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E6, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E13).
proofSteps: Reduce to complete A_0 with algebraically closed residue field (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions, the residue-field step) and choose the Cohen presentation (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/regular-local-cohen-presentation).
Unramified case: A is integral perfectoid over K° (PerfectoidSpaces:P1/integral-perfectoid-comparison, PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/bhatt-field-integral-model-comparison).

Ramified case: P_0 → P_m is faithfully flat, so A_0 → A′ is faithfully flat; g^p ≡ f modulo p gives g^p = f + ph = p(1 + h) with h without constant term, so u = 1 + h is a unit; A′[1/p] is a perfectoid Tate ring in the generalised sense (PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra/semiperfectoid-quasisyntomic-and-qrsp-rings) and the Scholze–Weinstein argument gives π with π^p = pv.

A′[1/p] → A′[1/p][v^{1/p^∞}] is ind-finite étale; almost purity (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale) makes A an integral perfectoid ring, π-torsion-free, with A′ → A almost faithfully flat modulo π; the roots of p come from π and v. Pass to almost elements (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-hom-and-adjoints).
acceptance: For A_0 = ℤ_p (d = 1, unramified) A is the p-adic completion of ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}], the valuation ring of K.

sources.match: Constructs, for a p-torsion-free Noetherian regular local A_0 of residue characteristic p, a map to an integral perfectoid algebra over Q_p(p^{1/p^∞})^: by adjoining p-power roots of p and of coordinates in the unramified case, and through A′, the unit v and almost purity in the ramified case.

nodes.title: The perfectoid cover is almost faithfully flat
nodes.statement: For A_0 → A as in DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/regular-local-perfectoid-cover and every A_0-module M: (a) Tor_i^{A_0}(M, A) is almost zero (killed by every p^{1/p^n}) for i > 0; (b) if M ⊗_{A_0} A is almost zero then M = 0. In the unramified case A_0 → A is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: Almost mathematics is with respect to p^{1/p^∞}A, which equals π^{1/p^∞}A and the radical of pA.
proofSteps: Factor A_0 → A′ → A_{!!} → A, where A_{!!} is the left adjoint of almostification applied to A (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-algebra-lower-shriek-shriek); A_{!!} → A is an injective almost isomorphism, A_{!!} is p-adically complete and p-torsion-free.

Formation of (·)_{!!} commutes with reduction modulo p^m, and A′ → A is almost faithfully flat modulo π, so A′ → A_{!!} is faithfully flat modulo p^m (PerfectoidSpaces:P0/lower-shriek-shriek-faithful-flatness); by Bhatt's Proposition 5.1 (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1/ordinary-flatness-from-complete-flatness) A_0 → A_{!!} is faithfully flat. This gives (a).

(b): reduce by faithful flatness and a filtration to M = A_0/I; then π^{1/p^n} ∈ IA_{!!} for all n, so p = π^p v^{-1} ∈ I^{p^n}A_{!!} and, by faithful flatness, p ∈ I^{p^n} for all n. Krull's intersection theorem (Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing) forces I = A_0 since p ≠ 0.
acceptance: For M = A_0/m the conclusion (b) says m A is not almost equal to A: the roots of p do not all lie in mA up to almost zero error.

nodes.title: Detection of the splitting obstruction after perfectoid base change
nodes.statement: Let A_0 be a complete Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p), Q_0 a perfect complex of A_0-modules and α_0 ∈ Hom_{D(A_0)}(Q_0, A_0[1]); put P = RHom_{A_0}(Q_0, A_0). Let g ∈ A_0 be nonzero in A_0/p, A_0 → A_{∞,0} the perfectoid cover (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/regular-local-perfectoid-cover) and A_{∞,0} → A_∞ Bhatt's root extension of g (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3/bhatt-perfectoid-root-extension), and write α_∞/p^m for the derived base change of α_0 modulo p^m. If α_0 ≠ 0, then there are m ≥ 3 with α_0/p^m ≠ 0 and k ≥ 0 such that (pg)^{1/p^k} does not annihilate α_∞/p^m in Hom_{D(A_∞)}(Q_0 ⊗^L A_∞, A_∞/p^m[1]).
hypotheses: For the direct summand theorem Q_0 = B_0/A_0 in degree 0, which is perfect because A_0 is regular (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/regular-local-finite-pd); for the derived theorem Q_0 is the cone of A_0 → RΓ(X_0, O) (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/proper-cohomology-perfect).
m ≥ 3 is used so that p²g ≠ 0 in A_0/p^m.
proofSteps: For P = RHom(Q_0,A_0), the triangle for multiplication by p^m gives 0 → H¹(P)/p^m → H¹(P ⊗^L A_0/p^m) → H²(P)[p^m] → 0. Transitions on the last term are multiplication by p. The p-primary torsion in finite H²(P) is bounded, so that tower is pro-zero. This proves the needed complex comparison directly from finite cohomology, rather than attributing a complex theorem to the finite-module Hom supplier.
Krull's intersection theorem for the finite module H¹(P) gives m ≥ 3 with α_0/p^m ≠ 0, so Ann(α_0/p^m) ≠ A_0/p^m; Krull again gives k with p²g ∉ (Ann(α_0/p^m))^{p^k}.

Choose a bounded finite free representative of Q_0. Tensor its dual modulo p^m along the two almost faithfully flat maps. The finite filtration, or its Tor spectral sequence, identifies cohomology after tensoring up to an almost isomorphism. This proves the almost Hom comparison for this perfect Q_0; arbitrary complexes are not covered by a module-only flatness assertion.
Annihilators therefore satisfy pg ∉ (Ann(α_∞/p^m))^{p^k}, losing one power of p in passing to almost mathematics, hence (pg)^{1/p^k} ∉ Ann(α_∞/p^m).
acceptance: If α_0 = 0 there is nothing to prove; the theorem is used contrapositively: almost vanishing of α_∞/p^m for (pg)^{1/p^∞} forces α_0 = 0.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.4, second and third paragraphs, p. 10
sources.match: Reduces to α_0/p^m ≠ 0 for some m ≥ 3, uses Krull's theorem to get k with p²g ∉ (Ann α_0/p^m)^{p^k}, and transports this through the almost faithfully flat maps A_0/p^m → A_{∞,0}/p^m → A_∞/p^m to (pg)^{1/p^k} ∉ Ann(α_∞/p^m).
Repeats the argument for the derived obstruction, where Q_0 is a perfect complex.
A → A_∞ is almost faithfully flat modulo t, which makes the second base change lossless.

nodes.title: Almost splitting on the annuli A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩
nodes.statement: In the setting of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/obstruction-detection, let A_0 → B_0 be finite and injective with B_0[1/(pg)] finite étale over A_0[1/(pg)], and let A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩ be the annular tower of A_∞ (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.1/annular-tower, with t = p). For fixed m, n ≥ 1 the base change A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩ → B_0 ⊗^L_{A_0} A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩ is almost split with respect to p^{1/p^∞}; hence the image of α_∞/p^m in Hom_{D(A_∞)}(Q_∞, A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m[1]) is almost zero for p^{1/p^∞}.
hypotheses: g divides p^n in A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩, so after inverting p the base change of A_0 → B_0 is finite étale.
proofSteps: Since g | p^n in A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩, the algebra B_0 ⊗ A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩[1/p] is finite étale over the perfectoid Tate ring A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩[1/p].

Almost purity (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale) dominates the base change by an almost finite étale cover of A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩, which is almost split (the trace of an almost finite étale algebra, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-dual-and-trace; Bhatt, Almost direct summands, Lemma 2.7).
Almost splitting passes to the reduction modulo p^m and kills the image of the obstruction up to p^{1/p^∞}.
acceptance: For g = 1 the annular tower is constant and the statement is the almost splitting of Faltings' almost purity case (André B §0.4).

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.4, fourth paragraph, p. 10
sources.match: As g divides p^n in A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩, the base change of A_0 → B_0 is finite étale after inverting p; almost purity dominates it by an almost finite étale cover, which is almost split, so the image of α_∞/p^m in the limit of the Hom groups over the annuli is almost zero.

nodes.title: From the annuli back to A_∞: the limit argument
nodes.statement: In the setting of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/obstruction-detection, put Q_∞ = Q_0 ⊗^L_{A_0} A_∞. If for every n ≥ 1 the image of α_∞/p^m in Hom_{D(A_∞)}(Q_∞, A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m[1]) is almost zero for p^{1/p^∞}, then α_∞/p^m is almost zero for (pg)^{1/p^∞}.
hypotheses: Q_0 is perfect, so RHom_{A_∞}(Q_∞, A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m) = K ⊗^L_{A_∞/p^m} A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m with K = RHom_{A_∞}(Q_∞, A_∞/p^m).
proofSteps: Represent K by a bounded complex of finite projective A_∞/p^m-modules, using perfection of Q_0. RA.1’s general quantitative Riemann comparison applies to the coefficient modules. Tensoring its cone with K and filtering by the finitely many terms preserves almost-pro-zero cohomology; RA.0’s linear-functor input and idempotence of the root ideal absorb the finitely many losses. The bound may depend on the finite amplitude; no statement uniform over all complexes is used.

Consequently each relevant cohomology tower, including degree zero, is almost-pro-isomorphic to a constant tower. The degree-zero tower has almost-zero lim¹ by RA.0’s derived-limit theorem; the resulting map Hom(Q_∞,A_∞/p^m[1]) → lim_n Hom(Q_∞,A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m[1]) is an almost isomorphism for (pg)^{1/p^∞}.

Each compatible component of the obstruction is annihilated by every root of p, hence by every root of pg; the limit has the same property. Almost injectivity of the comparison, and idempotence of the root ideal, make the original obstruction almost zero.
acceptance: For Q_0 = B_0/A_0 this is the last paragraph of the proof of Theorem 5.4; for the cone of A_0 → RΓ(X_0, O) it is the corresponding step of Theorem 6.1.

nodes.title: Bhatt's direct summand theorem for complete regular local rings
nodes.statement: Every complete Noetherian regular local ring A_0 of mixed characteristic (0, p), ramified or not, is a splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splinter).
hypotheses: Theorem 5.4 of Bhatt is stated for regular A_0 and a finite extension A_0 → B_0 (misprint DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E7, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E10); the reduction to the complete local case is DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions.
proofSteps: Reduce to B_0 a domain finite over A_0 with a discriminant g nonzero in A_0/p (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions).

The obstruction α_0 of A_0 → B_0 (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splitting-obstruction) has perfect cone B_0/A_0. If α_0 ≠ 0, DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/obstruction-detection gives m, k with (pg)^{1/p^k} ∉ Ann(α_∞/p^m).

DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/annular-almost-splitting and DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/obstruction-limit show α_∞/p^m is almost zero for (pg)^{1/p^∞}, a contradiction. Hence α_0 = 0 and A_0 → B_0 splits.
acceptance: For p odd, A_0 = ℤ_p⟦x⟧ and B_0 = A_0[y]/(y² − x − p): the discriminant is 4(x + p), so g = x + p, which is nonzero modulo p, and the theorem gives a splitting (here also visible directly, B_0 being free with basis 1, y).

sources.match: Proves the splitting of A_0 → B_0 for regular A_0 by reducing to the mixed characteristic regular local case, choosing a discriminant g, and showing that the obstruction class becomes almost zero after the base change to A_∞ through the annular tower and the quantitative Riemann extension theorem.
States the direct summand theorem and outlines this proof, which replaces the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma by the quantitative Riemann extension theorem.

nodes.title: Almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras
nodes.statement: Let (B, m_B) be a Noetherian local ring of residue characteristic p and dimension d, x = (x_1, …, x_d) a system of parameters, and D a B-algebra containing a nonzerodivisor π with a compatible system of p-power roots π^{1/p^h} (π^{1/p^0} = π, (π^{1/p^{h+1}})^p = π^{1/p^h}). Put J = Σ_h π^{1/p^h}D. D is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x, π^{1/p^∞}) if J ⊄ m_B D and J annihilates ((x_1, …, x_i)D :_D x_{i+1}) / (x_1, …, x_i)D for every 0 ≤ i < d.
hypotheses: Almostness is with respect to the ideal J generated by the roots of π, which need not be a valuation ideal: in André's application π = ϖg (source footnote 6).
The roots are data; the condition depends on the root system only through J.
proofSteps: The condition J ⊄ m_B D says that D is not almost equal to m_B D in the setup (D, J).
If D is big Cohen–Macaulay for x and π^{1/p^h} ∉ m_B D for some h, D is almost Cohen–Macaulay; conversely almost Cohen–Macaulay with J = D (π a unit) is big Cohen–Macaulay.
acceptance: The algebra D = B° of André B (18) is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x, (ϖg)^{1/p^∞}) (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/mixed-char-big-cm-existence).

sources.match: Defines almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras for (B, x, π^{1/p^∞}) by: m_B D does not contain π^{1/p^∞}, and the colon modules ((x_1, …, x_i)D : x_{i+1}D)/(x_1, …, x_i)D are killed by π^{1/p^∞}; the footnote stresses that π = ϖg is not a valuation-theoretic setup.

nodes.title: Hochster's partial algebra modifications
nodes.statement: Let (R,m) be Noetherian local, x a system of parameters, and (M,e) an R-module with a distinguished element e. For 0 ≤ k < length x, a relation x_{k+1}u_{k+1} = Σ_{j≤k} x_j u_j in M, and N ≥ 1, set M[X] = M ⊗_R R[X_1,…,X_k], F = u_{k+1} − Σ_{j≤k} x_j(e X_j), and M′ = M[X]_{≤N}/F·R[X]_{≤N−1}. Constants give a pointed map (M,e) → (M′,e′). A finite sequence starting at an algebra T carries e=1 and is bad when the final image of e lies in m times the final module. A double sequence along a local map (R,m) → (S,n) first modifies over R and then over S after tensoring, carrying 1 ⊗ e; badness is tested against n at the end.
hypotheses: The distinguished element supplies the coefficient of each formal variable. An unpointed arbitrary module has no element 1. The notation in Hochster §4.1 p. 8 and Heitmann–Ma §1.2 p. 3 suppresses this datum (E22).
Only scalar polynomials multiply F; there is no multiplication on M. This also repairs André’s coefficient-module slip E11.

At a fixed relation the N-colimit is M[X]/F·R[X], as a module. For an algebra T this need not equal T[X]/(F·T[X]); E21 gives a counterexample. The comparison of finite bad witnesses with full algebra modifications is the separate gap G4.
proofSteps: F is now an element of M[X] of degree at most one. Multiplication by polynomials of degree at most N−1 has image in degree at most N, so the quotient and its pointed constant map are well defined.
The class of F vanishes, so the image of u_{k+1} equals Σ x_j times the class of eX_j. Pointed maps compatible with the relation induce maps of these quotients.

Taking the filtered colimit over N gives exactly M[X]/F·R[X]. Do not infer an algebra structure or the full modification criterion from this fixed-relation colimit; the required finite-witness comparison is G4.
acceptance: For an R-algebra T on which x is weakly regular, choose v_j with u_{k+1}=Σ x_jv_j. Polynomial evaluation X_j↦v_j is an R-linear retraction of the partial modification back to T. Its complement need not be free. This assertion is not made for an arbitrary pointed module.

sources.match: Defines the scalar-polynomial quotient and bad finite sequences. E21 corrects the fixed-relation colimit assertion, and E22 supplies the distinguished coefficient needed for its module notation; G4 retains the full-algebra comparison as a proof obligation.
Recalls partial modifications and double sequences; interpret the formal variables with the transported distinguished element as in E22. Theorem 1.6 is on pp. 3–4.
Recalls degree-bounded module modifications; E11 repairs multiplication by the coefficient module, with the pointed convention of E22.

nodes.title: Hochster's modification criterion for (weakly functorial) big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) → (S, n) be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with systems of parameters x of R and y of S, and T an R-algebra. There is a commutative square R → B → C, R → S → C, with R → B factoring through T, B a big Cohen–Macaulay R-algebra for x and C a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay S-algebra, if and only if there is no bad double sequence of partial algebra modifications (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/partial-algebra-modification) of T over R → S. Taking S = R and m-adic completions: a Noetherian local ring R has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra iff no sequence of partial algebra modifications of R is bad.
hypotheses: The system of parameters is fixed throughout, as in Heitmann–Ma Theorem 1.6; Hochster's Theorem 4.2 allows it to vary.

The intended criterion is stated in Hochster Theorem 4.2 and Heitmann–Ma Theorem 1.6. Its comparison with the explicitly pointed quotient in the preceding node is G4, not a consequence of taking a fixed-relation N-colimit.
proofSteps: Construct B′ as the direct limit of all finite sequences of algebra modifications of T over R, and C′ as the direct limit of algebra modifications of S ⊗_R B′ over S; x and y are weakly regular on B′ and C′ by construction.

The nontrivial finite-witness comparison must show that any bad witness in the full algebra-modification construction is realised by a finite pointed partial sequence (and similarly for double sequences). This is G4. The fixed-relation colimit claim is false (E21) and cannot prove this step. Conversely a map to a big Cohen–Macaulay algebra extends along partial modifications by evaluating the formal variables, so no such sequence is bad.

Subject to the finite-witness comparison G4, nonbadness gives nonzero maximal-ideal quotients of B′ and C′. Complete using the arbitrary-module theorem G3. The map extends from the m-adic completion of B′ to the n-adic completion of C′ because the base map is local.
acceptance: If R is Cohen–Macaulay, R itself is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra and no sequence starting at R is bad.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.2 and the paragraph before it, p. 9 of the author preprint
sources.match: For a local map R → S and an R-algebra T, a commutative square with B big Cohen–Macaulay for R through T and C balanced big Cohen–Macaulay for S exists iff there is no bad double sequence of partial algebra modifications of T over R → S.

nodes.title: Hochster's key lemma: extending maps along partial modifications
nodes.statement: Let R be a local ring, (M,e) a pointed R-module, T an R-algebra, c ∈ T a nonzerodivisor and α : M → T[1/c] an R-linear map with α(e)=1 and α(M) ⊆ c^{-N}T. Let M → M′ be a partial algebra modification with respect to x_1, …, x_{k+1} with degree bound D. Suppose that for every relation x_{k+1}t_{k+1} = Σ_{j≤k} x_j t_j with t_j ∈ T one has c·t_{k+1} ∈ (x_1, …, x_k)T. Then α extends to an R-linear β : M′ → T[1/c] with β(M′) ⊆ c^{-(ND+D+N)}T. The extension satisfies β(e′)=1 for the transported distinguished element.
hypotheses: The map is pointed from the outset. With F=u_{k+1}−Σ x_j(eX_j), the evaluation argument kills F because α(e)=1; this is the convention required by E22.
proofSteps: Apply α to the defining relation: x_{k+1}v_{k+1} = Σ x_j v_j with v_j = α(u_j) ∈ c^{-N}T, so x_{k+1}(c^N v_{k+1}) = Σ x_j (c^N v_j) and the hypothesis gives c^{N+1}v_{k+1} = Σ x_j w_j with w_j ∈ T.

Use X_j ↦ w_j/c^{N+1} to evaluate polynomials in T[1/c], and define γ(uX^a)=α(u)∏(w_j/c^{N+1})^{a_j}. It is R-linear and semilinear for polynomial evaluation. Because α(e)=1, γ(F)=0, so γ kills F·R[X]_{≤D−1} and preserves the distinguished element. No R[X]-module structure on the target with unevaluated variables is presumed.
β is γ restricted to M[X]_{≤D}; each monomial contributes at worst c^{-N}·c^{-(N+1)D} = c^{-(ND+D+N)}.
acceptance: If c is a unit, its annihilation condition is the equality of the indicated parameter colon with the preceding parameter ideal; the evaluated extension lands in T itself.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.1 and its proof, pp. 9–10 of the author preprint
sources.match: States and proves the extension of α : M → T_c along a partial algebra modification of degree bound D with image in c^{-(ND+D+N)}T, under the hypothesis that c kills the parameter colon obstructions in T.
Applies Hochster's Lemma 5.1 with c = π^{1/p^m} for arbitrary m.

nodes.title: Almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras give balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
nodes.statement: Let B be a Noetherian local ring of residue characteristic p. If B has an almost Cohen–Macaulay algebra D for (B, x, π^{1/p^∞}) (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/almost-big-cm-algebra) for some system of parameters x and some root system of a nonzerodivisor π of D, then B has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra.
hypotheses: The proof gives maps M_ℓ → π^{-1/p^h}D ⊂ D[1/π] depending on the choices, not a B-algebra map from the colimit to D: André's parenthetical claim that B → D factors through the big Cohen–Macaulay algebra is dropped (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E12, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E19).
The exponent h of π^{-1/p^h} is distinct from the degree bound n of the modifications; it is made small by choosing c = π^{1/p^m} with m large compared with n and ℓ.
proofSteps: Fix a finite sequence B = M_1 → ⋯ → M_ℓ of partial modifications of degree ≤ n and h ≥ 0. With c = π^{1/p^m}, m ≫ n, ℓ, h, the almost Cohen–Macaulay property says c kills the parameter colon obstructions in D, so DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/hochster-key-lemma extends B → D step by step to compatible maps M_t → π^{-1/p^h}D sending 1 to 1.
If the image of 1 lay in m_B M_ℓ, then 1 ∈ m_B π^{-1/p^h}D, i.e. π^{1/p^h} ∈ m_B D, contradicting J ⊄ m_B D for h large. So no sequence is bad.
By DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/modification-criterion (with S = R = B) there is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra.
acceptance: If D is already big Cohen–Macaulay for x the conclusion is DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/completion-balances.

sources.match: From an almost Cohen–Macaulay algebra D for (B, x, π^{1/p^∞}), Hochster's crucial lemma with c = π^{1/p^m} builds maps from finite sequences of partial modifications to π^{-1/p^n}D, shows none is bad since m_B D does not contain π^{1/p^∞}, and completes the colimit to a Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra.
The two inputs: the extension lemma and the no-bad-sequence criterion.

nodes.title: Criteria for almost Cohen–Macaulayness
nodes.statement: Let B be a Noetherian local ring of residue characteristic p, A ⊆ B a Cohen–Macaulay local subring with B finite over A, x ⊂ A a system of parameters of B, and D a B-algebra with a nonzerodivisor π and a root system. Then D is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x, π^{1/p^∞}) iff it is so for (A, x, π^{1/p^∞}). This holds in each of the following cases: (a) (πD) ∩ A ≠ 0 and D is almost isomorphic, in the setup (A[π^{1/p^∞}], π^{1/p^∞}A[π^{1/p^∞}]), to a faithfully flat A-algebra D′ (not necessarily containing B); (b) (πD) ∩ A ⊄ x_1A, D has no x_1-torsion, and D/x_1D is almost isomorphic in the same setup to a faithfully flat A/x_1A-algebra.
hypotheses: Almost isomorphism is in the setup generated by the roots of π, which acts on D′ through the almost isomorphism.
proofSteps: m_A B is m_B-primary, so J ⊄ m_B D iff J ⊄ m_A D: the first assertion.

(a): if J ⊆ m_A D, transport to D′ and apply PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/krull-detection-lemma with R = A, S = D′, M = A/m_A: K = J D′ is idempotent, kills M ⊗ D′ and contains a nonzero element of A, so M = 0, absurd. Colon modules vanish on D′ by flatness and A Cohen–Macaulay, hence are almost zero on D.
(b): the same with A/x_1A (Cohen–Macaulay) and (x_2, …, x_d), using that x_1 is regular on D.
acceptance: André's application uses (b) with x_1 = p² and π = ϖg, where (π) ∩ A = pgA ⊄ p²A.

sources.match: Shows almost Cohen–Macaulayness for (B, x) and (A, x) agree, and that it holds when D (resp. D/x_1D) is almost isomorphic to a faithfully flat A- (resp. A/x_1A-) algebra under the conditions on (π) ∩ A, using Lemme 1.1.2 and flatness.

nodes.title: Reductions for the existence of big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
nodes.statement: Let (B, m_B) be a Noetherian local ring. (1) If P is a minimal prime with dim B/P = dim B, a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B/P-algebra is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra. (2) A balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B̂-algebra is one for B. (3) If B is complete and p-torsion-free with residue characteristic p, then B_red is p-torsion-free and a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B_red-algebra is one for B. (4) If B is complete with residue field k and coefficient map Λ = C(k) → B, then B′ = (B ⊗_Λ W(k^{1/p^∞}))^ is complete Noetherian local, faithfully flat over B with m_B B′ = m_{B′}, and a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B′-algebra is one for B.
hypotheses: In (1) the dimension condition matters: a system of parameters of B maps to one of B/P only when dim B/P = dim B.
proofSteps: (1) and (2): systems of parameters of B map to systems of parameters of B/P (equal dimension) and of B̂, and m_B C ≠ C is preserved.
(3): nilpotents are killed in a reduced quotient; p-torsion-freeness of B_red follows from that of B.

(4): DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/perfect-residue-completed-basechange gives B′ with m_B B′ = m_{B′}; a system of parameters of B is one of B′ because B → B′ is flat local with zero-dimensional closed fibre.
acceptance: For B = ℤ_p⟦x, y⟧/(xy) the reduction (1) passes to B/(x) ≅ ℤ_p⟦y⟧, which is its own balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra.

sources.match: One may complete, divide by the nilradical, and replace B by the faithfully flat extension B ⊗̂_Λ W(k^{1/p^∞}).
The equal-characteristic case being known, the mixed characteristic p-torsion-free case is the one treated.

nodes.title: André's existence theorem for big Cohen–Macaulay algebras in mixed characteristic
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian local ring B of mixed characteristic (0, p) (residue characteristic p) has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra.
hypotheses: B may have p-torsion. Complete first and choose a minimal prime P with dim(B̂/P)=dim B. If p∈P, use the characteristic-p existence theorem on B̂/P, even when p was not nilpotent in B. Otherwise the quotient is a p-torsion-free mixed-characteristic domain.
proofSteps: Complete and take a maximal-dimensional domain quotient as just described. In the mixed-characteristic case pass faithfully flatly to a perfect residue field, then choose a maximal-dimensional minimal-prime quotient again if needed: the extension is still p-torsion-free, so its minimal primes avoid p. Systems of parameters from the original ring remain systems of parameters throughout. The characteristic-p branch is DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/char-p-absolute-integral-closure.

Choose a system of parameters x with x_1 = p²; B is finite over A = W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧, T_i ↦ x_{i+1} (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/finite-parameter-subring), injectively for B a domain; choose g ∈ A ∖ pA with B[1/(pg)] étale over A[1/(pg)] (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions).

Let D = B° be the integral closure of Â°_∞∞ in B ⊗_A Â_∞∞[1/g] and π^{1/p^m} = (ϖg)^{1/p^m}, a nonzerodivisor on D. Then (π) ∩ A = pgA ⊄ p²A, D is p-torsion-free, and D/p²D is almost isomorphic in the setup ((Â°_∞∞)_{!!}, (ϖg)^{1/p^∞}) to (D/p²D)^a_{!!}, which is faithfully flat over A/p² by André's flatness theorem and its ramified form (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/kummer-almost-faithful-flatness, PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/ramified-kummer-almost-flatness, PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/flat-integral-model).
