Every Noetherian local ring B has a Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra, i.e. a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra.

nodes.title: Hochster–Huneke: R⁺ is big Cohen–Macaulay in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let (R, m) be a Noetherian local domain of characteristic p > 0 that is a homomorphic image of a Gorenstein local ring (for example a complete local domain), and R⁺ its absolute integral closure (the integral closure of R in an algebraic closure of Frac R). Then H^i_m(R⁺) = 0 for i < dim R, and every system of parameters of R is a regular sequence on R⁺; R⁺ ≠ mR⁺, so R⁺ is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay R-algebra.
hypotheses: Hochster–Huneke prove it for excellent R; Huneke–Lyubeznik for homomorphic images of Gorenstein local rings, with a simpler proof; complete local domains satisfy both.
proofSteps: Apply the strong form of Huneke–Lyubeznik Theorem 2.1 to every finite intermediate domain R′ ⊆ R⁺: for each i<dim R there is a finite R′-extension inside R⁺ killing H^i_m(R′). Finite extensions have the same dimension; the theorem’s stated finite-extension form supplies this step. Its proof uses Frobenius, local duality over the Gorenstein ring and the equational Lemma 2.2.

Every class in the filtered colimit of H^i_m(R′) thus dies at a later finite stage, so H^i_m(R⁺)=0. This uses local cohomology commuting with filtered colimits and its Čech comparison; merely killing the classes coming from R would not suffice.
Corollary 2.3(b): induction on j shows x_1, …, x_j is regular on R⁺, using the local cohomology vanishing and the identification of the colon modules.
R⁺ ≠ mR⁺ because R⁺ is integral over R (lying over).
acceptance: For R = 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧ (regular), R⁺ is faithfully flat over R, consistent with DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/regular-big-cm-flat.
In equal characteristic 0 and dim R ≥ 3 the analogous statement is false: a trace argument shows R⁺ is not big Cohen–Macaulay (BMPSTWW §2.2).

sources.match: For a Noetherian local domain of characteristic p that is a homomorphic image of a Gorenstein local ring, local cohomology below the dimension dies in a finite extension; consequently H^i_m(R⁺) = 0 for i < dim R and every system of parameters is a regular sequence on R⁺.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.5 and the paragraph after it, p. 13
sources.match: States the theorem in characteristic p (Hochster–Huneke 1992, Theorem 1.1) and the failure of the analogue in equal characteristic 0 of dimension ≥ 3.

nodes.title: Big Cohen–Macaulay algebras in equal characteristic zero
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian local ring containing ℚ has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra.
hypotheses: Existence only: R⁺ itself is not big Cohen–Macaulay in equal characteristic 0 and dimension ≥ 3 (BMPSTWW §2.2).

The source (Hochster–Huneke 1995) was not read in this job; the outline below is the classical reduction to characteristic p through the finitely many equations of a bad sequence, and the step from a complete local ring to a finitely generated algebra rests on Artin–Popescu approximation. This is recorded as gap G1.
proofSteps: Reduce to B a complete local domain (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/big-cm-reductions).

By the modification criterion (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/modification-criterion) it suffices to show no sequence of partial algebra modifications of B is bad. A bad sequence is witnessed by finitely many elements and equations.

Descend the bad sequence to a local ring essentially of finite type over a finitely generated ℤ-algebra, using Néron–Popescu desingularisation (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/popescu-desingularization) and limit arguments (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/finite-presentation-limits), keeping the parameters a system of parameters on a dense open set of the base.

Reduce modulo a suitable maximal ideal of the base to obtain a bad sequence over a Noetherian local ring of characteristic p whose completion has a domain quotient of maximal dimension, contradicting DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/char-p-absolute-integral-closure.
acceptance: For B regular containing ℚ, B is its own balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra; the theorem is used for singular local rings such as the complete local domains S_{m,i} in André's proof of Théorème 0.7.2.

sources.match: Balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras exist in equal characteristic by Hochster–Huneke [HH92, HH95] and in mixed characteristic by André.
Cites the equal-characteristic case as known ([17] = Hochster–Huneke 1995) and uses it in the proof of Théorème 0.7.2.

nodes.title: Every Noetherian local ring has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian local ring B has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/balanced-big-cm-module).
hypotheses: Characteristic types: equal characteristic p (Hochster–Huneke), equal characteristic 0 (Hochster–Huneke), mixed characteristic (André).
proofSteps: Reduce to B complete with a minimal prime of maximal dimension, then to the corresponding complete local domain (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/big-cm-reductions).
Equal characteristic p: R⁺ of the complete local domain (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/char-p-absolute-integral-closure).
Equal characteristic 0: DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/equal-char-zero-big-cm.
Mixed characteristic: DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/mixed-char-big-cm-existence.
acceptance: Consequence (monomial theorem): for every system of parameters x of B and t ≥ 1, (x_1⋯x_d)^{t−1} ∉ (x_1^t, …, x_d^t)B (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/homological-consequences).

sources.match: Every Noetherian local ring has a Cohen–Macaulay algebra; the equal-characteristic case is known and the mixed characteristic case is proved in §4.2.

nodes.title: Weak functoriality from squares of almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras
nodes.statement: Let β : B → B′ be a local homomorphism of complete local domains of mixed characteristic (0, p), with systems of parameters x of B and x′ of B′. Suppose β fits in a commutative square B → D, B′ → D′, δ : D → D′, where D is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x, π^{1/p^∞}), D′ is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B′, x′, π′^{1/p^∞}), and δ(π^{1/p^m}) divides π′^{1/p^m} in D′ for every m. Then β fits in a commutative square B → C, B′ → C′, γ : C → C′ with C and C′ balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras for B and B′.
hypotheses: D′ is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B′, x′, π′^{1/p^∞}), not for B (misprint DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E13, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E3).
proofSteps: By DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/modification-criterion it suffices to show no double sequence of partial algebra modifications of B over B → B′ is bad.

Extend B → D along the B-part with denominators π^{-1/p^h} and then B′ ⊗ M_r → D′ along the B′-part with denominators π′^{-1/p^h}, using DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/hochster-key-lemma twice; the divisibility δ(π^{1/p^m}) | π′^{1/p^m} transports the first denominators into the second.
Badness would put π′^{1/p^h} into m_{B′}D′ for large h, contradicting almost Cohen–Macaulayness of D′.
acceptance: For β = id and D = D′ this is DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/almost-cm-to-big-cm.

sources.match: If β fits in a square of almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras D → D′ with δ(π^{1/p^m}) dividing π′^{1/p^m}, then it fits in a square of Cohen–Macaulay algebras, by the same technique of partial modifications.
The double-sequence criterion for weakly functorial squares along a local map.

nodes.title: The direct summand theorem
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian regular ring is a splinter: for a Noetherian regular ring R and a commutative R-algebra S that is finite and faithful as an R-module, R → S admits an R-linear retraction (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/split-algebra). Equivalently, every finite extension of R is pure, and S is a generator of the category of R-modules.
hypotheses: The retraction is R-linear and is not required to be multiplicative.
The theorem is stated once; it has two proofs in mixed characteristic, André's and Bhatt's, recorded as alternative routes in the proof steps. Both routes use the same reductions.
proofSteps: Reduce to A a complete regular local ring with algebraically closed residue field and S a domain finite over A (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions).
A contains ℚ: trace splitting (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/trace-retraction). A has characteristic p: Frobenius (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.1/frobenius-direct-summand).
Mixed characteristic, Bhatt's route: DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/bhatt-direct-summand, valid for ramified and unramified A.

Mixed characteristic, André's route: A ⊆ S is dominated by a faithfully flat algebra (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/finite-cover-flat-domination, built from André's big Cohen–Macaulay algebras over the unramified ring W(k)⟦T⟧ of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/mixed-char-big-cm-existence); then A → S is pure as a left factor of a faithfully flat map, hence split since S is finite (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map). For A unramified this is also André's direct theorem DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.2/andre-unramified-direct-summand.
acceptance: Dimension ≤ 2 (any characteristic) is DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/low-dimension-direct-summand; dimension 3 in mixed characteristic is Heitmann's theorem, a special case.
Regularity cannot be weakened to normality: in characteristic p or mixed characteristic there are normal non-splinters, and K[x, y]/(xy) is a reduced non-splinter (André B §0.2).

sources.match: States Hochster's direct summand conjecture for Noetherian regular rings and proves it, the general case following from the case W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧ by Hochster's reduction.
Flat domination of finite covers gives purity of R → S, hence the conjecture again by a detour.
Proves the direct summand theorem for every regular A_0 by a proof avoiding the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma.

nodes.title: Products of flat modules over a Noetherian ring are flat
nodes.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring (more generally a coherent ring) and (M_i)_{i∈I} any family of flat R-modules. Then ∏_i M_i is flat. If moreover each M_i is an R-algebra and for every maximal ideal m of R some M_i satisfies mM_i ≠ M_i, then ∏_i M_i is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: Tau Ceti has the finite case (Module.Flat.pi); the infinite case needs coherence (Chase's theorem), and fails over non-coherent rings.
proofSteps: Flatness is tested on finitely generated ideals J: J is finitely presented since R is Noetherian, so J ⊗ ∏ M_i ≅ ∏ (J ⊗ M_i) (tensor product with a finitely presented module commutes with arbitrary products).
J ⊗ M_i → M_i is injective for every i, hence so is the product map.
Faithful flatness: m(∏ M_i) ⊆ ∏ mM_i ≠ ∏ M_i when some factor has mM_i ≠ M_i, and flat with mT ≠ T for all maximal m is faithfully flat (Mathlib Module.FaithfullyFlat).
acceptance: For I finite this is Tau Ceti's Module.Flat.pi.
Over a non-coherent ring the statement fails (Chase); the Noetherian hypothesis is used exactly in the finite presentation of ideals.

sources.match: Uses that, R being Noetherian, the product T = ∏ T_{m,i} of flat R-algebras is still flat over R.

nodes.title: Finite covers of regular rings are dominated by faithfully flat algebras
nodes.statement: Let R be a Noetherian regular ring and R ⊆ S a finite extension. There is a commutative S-algebra T such that the composite R → S → T is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: The product is taken only over components that receive R̂_m injectively: André's proof takes all factors of the normalisation of S ⊗_R R̂_m, which can include components of smaller dimension over which Remarque 4.2.1 does not apply (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E14, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E20). No normalisation is needed: a domain quotient of maximal dimension suffices.
proofSteps: For each maximal ideal m of R, R̂_m is a complete regular local domain and S ⊗_R R̂_m is a finite R̂_m-algebra, a finite product of complete local rings (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/finite-algebra-completion-product); R̂_m → S ⊗ R̂_m is injective.
By lying over for the minimal prime 0 of R̂_m, some factor has a prime P lying over 0; S_m := factor/P is a complete local domain, finite over R̂_m and containing it, of the same dimension.

Let T_m be a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay S_m-algebra (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/big-cm-existence). It is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay R̂_m-algebra (same systems of parameters), hence faithfully flat over R̂_m (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/regular-big-cm-flat), hence flat over R with mT_m ≠ T_m.
T = ∏_m T_m is an S-algebra, flat over R (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/flat-products-noetherian) and faithfully flat because each maximal ideal stays proper in its own factor.
acceptance: For R a field the statement says every nonzero finite K-algebra S has a K-algebra map to a nonzero K-algebra: take a residue field of S.
Consequence: R → S is pure, hence split since S is finite (André B §0.7).

sources.match: For a Noetherian regular ring R and a finite extension R ⊆ S there is S → T with R → T faithfully flat; in particular R → S is pure.

Works over each completion R̂_m, takes Cohen–Macaulay algebras T_{m,i} for the complete local domain factors, uses Remarque 4.2.1 for faithful flatness over R̂_m, and takes the product over all m and i.

nodes.title: R → R⁺ splits for complete regular local rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian regular local ring and R⁺ the integral closure of R in an algebraic closure of Frac(R). Then R → R⁺ admits an R-linear retraction. In particular W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧ → W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧⁺ splits for every perfect field k of characteristic p.
hypotheses: Completeness of R is needed for the passage from purity to splitting: the corresponding statement for an arbitrary DVR V in place of W(k), asserted in André B Annexe A.3 Applications, fails by the Datta–Murayama example (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E4, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E21).
proofSteps: R⁺ is the filtered union of its finite R-subalgebras S_α, each split over R by the direct summand theorem (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/direct-summand-theorem), hence pure.
Filtered colimits of pure maps are pure (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map), so R → R⁺ is pure.
R is complete, so the pure map R → R⁺ splits (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.1/complete-pure-split).
acceptance: For R a complete DVR the retraction exists (R⁺ is the union of DVRs finite over R, each free); the theorem is substantial from dimension 2 on.

In characteristic p the splitting of R → R⁺ also follows from DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/regular-big-cm-flat and DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/char-p-absolute-integral-closure, which make R⁺ faithfully flat over R.

sources.match: The embedding of W(k)⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧ into its integral closure in an algebraic closure of its fraction field admits a W(k)⟦T⟧-linear retraction (cf. A.3).

Deduces the retraction of R → R⁺ from purity through the implication (a) ⇒ (b) of Proposition A.3.1, applied to R = V⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧ with σ raising the T_i to a fixed power; the completeness restriction of the corrected statement is needed.
The non-complete counterexample: an excellent Henselian DVR V with Hom_V(V^{1/p}, V) = 0.

nodes.title: Contracted ideals and the monomial theorem
nodes.statement: (1) Contracted ideals: for every Noetherian regular ring R, every ideal I of R and every injective integral ring map R → S, IS ∩ R = I. (2) Monomial theorem: for every Noetherian local ring R of dimension d ≥ 1, every system of parameters x_1, …, x_d and all m, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, (x_1⋯x_d)^m ∈ (x_1^n, …, x_d^n)R if and only if m ≥ n. In dimension 0 the empty product 1 is never in the zero ideal of a nonzero ring.
hypotheses: The 'if and only if' form of (2) needs d ≥ 1; André's §0.1(4) states it for every local ring, which fails for d = 0 (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E15, after PAPER-ANDRE-18-B/E9). The non-containment for m < n holds in all dimensions.
proofSteps: (1): R → S is pure (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splinter API isPure_of_isIntegral with the direct summand theorem DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/direct-summand-theorem), so R/I → S/IS is injective.
(2), m ≥ n: (x_1⋯x_d)^m is a multiple of x_1^n when m ≥ n and d ≥ 1.

(2), m < n: let C be a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay R-algebra (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/big-cm-existence). For a regular sequence x on C with C ≠ (x)C, (x_1⋯x_d)^{n−1} ∉ (x_1^n, …, x_d^n)C (Koszul/regular-sequence computation, the monomial API of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/big-cm-module); a fortiori not in the ideal of R.
acceptance: For R = K⟦x, y⟧/(xy) with system of parameters x + y, d = 1: (x + y)^m ∈ ((x + y)^n) iff m ≥ n.

André lists further equivalent or implied statements (descent of flatness along integral extensions, the improved new intersection theorem, the syzygy theorem) with references to Ohi, Hochster, Dutta and Evans–Griffith; they are not targets of this roadmap.

sources.match: Lists equivalent forms of the direct summand conjecture, including contraction of ideals from integral extensions and the monomial conjecture, with references for the equivalences; (1) ⇒ (2) is elementary from purity.

nodes.title: Purity survives completion and perfect residue fields
nodes.statement: Let β : B → B′ be a pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. Then the induced map B̂ → B̂′ of maximal-ideal-adic completions is pure. If B and B′ have mixed characteristic (0, p) and the residue extension k → k′ is separable, then for compatible coefficient maps Λ → B̂, Λ′ → B̂′ the map (B̂ ⊗_Λ W(k^{1/p^∞}))^ → (B̂′ ⊗_{Λ′} W(k′^{1/p^∞}))^ is pure.
hypotheses: Compatible coefficient rings exist because k → k′ is separable (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1/cohen-relative-separable-compatibility).
Request R2 to R03.1 is needed for the common coefficient extension; the current individual perfect-residue-basechange statement does not assert this comparison.
proofSteps: Put C=completion_{m_B B′}(B′). This is Noetherian local, and its maximal-adic completion is B̂′, faithfully flat over C. To prove B̂ → C pure, test every finite B̂-module P, rather than only those descending to B.

Each P/m_B^nP is a finite B-module and is unchanged by tensoring B → B̂ at that level. Purity of B → B′ gives its injection into (P/m_B^nP) ⊗_B B′ = (P/m_B^nP) ⊗_{B̂} C. An element in the kernel of P → P ⊗_{B̂} C therefore lies in every m_B^nP; Krull intersection for the finite B̂-module P makes it zero. Compose with C → B̂′.

For the perfect-residue assertion, compatibility of the two completed coefficient extensions is an additional supplier need R2. Separability makes k′ ⊗_k k^perf a field, but the existence and faithful flatness of the resulting map of completed Cohen extensions still need proof. Given that comparison, base change preserves purity and the first part handles completion. Individual faithfully flat extensions of source and target alone do not establish purity of the comparison map.
acceptance: A faithfully flat local map is pure and stays so after completion; a split local map stays split.

sources.locator: Annexe A.2, Lemme A.2.2 and proof, p. 90
sources.match: A pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings induces a pure map of completions, through the m_R S-adic completion and Krull's theorem.
The purity hypothesis is preserved by completion and passage to perfect residue fields by Lemme A.2.2.

nodes.title: Weak functoriality of big Cohen–Macaulay algebras for regular targets
nodes.statement: Let β : B → B′ be an injective local homomorphism of complete Noetherian local domains of mixed characteristic (0, p), with separable residue field extension k → k′ and B′ regular. Then there are a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra C, a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B′-algebra C′ and a ring map γ : C → C′ whose composite with B → C equals the composite of β with B′ → C′.
hypotheses: The three obstructions André lists all disappear under these hypotheses: (1) perfect residue fields are reached compatibly because k → k′ is separable; (2) no square A → A′ of unramified complete regular local rings finite under B → B′ exists in general — for B = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → B′ = ℤ_p⟦T, U⟧/(T² − TU + p) no parameter of B/p maps to a parameter of B′/p — but A′ may be ramified when B′ is regular; (3) the discriminant condition δ((ϖg)^{1/p^m}) | (ϖg′)^{1/p^m} is met by replacing g′ by g′β(g), which needs β(g) to be a nonzerodivisor, guaranteed by injectivity of β (β(g) = 0 when Spec B′[1/p] maps into the singular locus of Spec B[1/p]).
The flatness input over a ramified regular base B′ with several elements ramified is André B Remarque 2.6.1(4), requested from PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5 (request R1).

Passing to perfect residue fields must preserve injectivity through a common coefficient base change, followed by a faithfully flat target extension. This relative comparison is request R2 to R03.1, not a consequence of separate extensions of the two rings.
proofSteps: Pass to perfect residue fields through a common compatible coefficient extension (request R2 to R03.1), preserving injectivity by flat base change and faithful flatness on the target. Separate choices of the two residue extensions would not justify the new square.

Build A, A_∞, Â_∞∞ and D = B° for B as in DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/mixed-char-big-cm-existence, and A′ = B′ itself (regular, possibly ramified) with D′ = g^{-1/p^∞}Â′_∞⟨ζ_{p^∞}, g^{1/p^∞}, T^{1/p^∞}⟩°, which is integrally closed in D′[1/(pg)] by the perfectoid Riemann extension theorem (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.3/perfectoid-riemann-extension).

D′/p² is almost isomorphic to a faithfully flat B′/p²-algebra (André's flatness theorem over the ramified base B′, request R1 to PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5), so D′ is almost Cohen–Macaulay for B′ (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/almost-cm-criteria); D is almost Cohen–Macaulay for B as before, and the map δ : D → D′ exists with the divisibility after replacing g′ by g′β(g).
DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.4/weak-functoriality-almost-cm turns the square of almost Cohen–Macaulay algebras into a square of balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras.
acceptance: André's example ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → ℤ_p⟦T, U⟧/(T² − TU + p) ≅ ℤ_p⟦T, V⟧/(TV − p) (regular of dimension 2) is covered: the target is regular, so no unramified square is needed.
Heitmann–Ma remove the separability hypothesis by a different construction; that generalisation is not a target here.

sources.locator: §4.4, problems (1)–(3) and the paragraph after them, pp. 87–88
sources.match: Shows the weak functoriality problem has a positive answer when β is injective, k → k′ separable and B′ regular, constructing D′ := g^{-1/p^∞}Â′_∞⟨ζ_{p^∞}, g^{1/p^∞}, T^{1/p^∞}⟩° and applying Proposition 4.4.1.
The flatness method allows several ramified elements and a ramified complete regular local base with perfect residue field.

nodes.title: Cohen–Macaulayness descends along pure maps to regular rings with a big Cohen–Macaulay square
nodes.statement: Let β : B → B′ be a pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with B′ regular. Suppose there are a B-algebra C on which some system of parameters x = (x_1, …, x_d) of B is a regular sequence, a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B′-algebra C′ and a ring map C → C′ compatible with β. Then x is a regular sequence on B; in particular B is Cohen–Macaulay.
hypotheses: André calls this 'a known argument' and cites Hochster–Huneke 1995 (2.3), which was not read in this job; the steps below are a complete argument from this roadmap's nodes.
proofSteps: Let 0 ≤ i < d and b ∈ B with x_{i+1}b ∈ (x_1, …, x_i)B. As x is regular on C, b ∈ (x_1, …, x_i)C, hence b ∈ (x_1, …, x_i)C′.
C′ is faithfully flat over the regular local ring B′ (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/regular-big-cm-flat), so (x_1, …, x_i)C′ ∩ B′ = (x_1, …, x_i)B′ and b ∈ (x_1, …, x_i)B′.
B → B′ is pure, so (x_1, …, x_i)B′ ∩ B = (x_1, …, x_i)B (PerfectoidSpacesPartII:RA.5/pure-map) and b ∈ (x_1, …, x_i)B. Since x is a system of parameters, B ≠ (x)B, and B is Cohen–Macaulay.
acceptance: For B = B′ regular and C = C′ = B the conclusion is that regular local rings are Cohen–Macaulay.

sources.match: Deduces Théorème 4.4.2 from weak functoriality by a known argument (Hochster–Huneke 1995, (2.3)), noting that purity is preserved by completion and perfect residue fields.

nodes.title: Pure subrings of regular rings are Cohen–Macaulay (mixed characteristic, separable residue extension)
nodes.statement: Let B → B′ be a pure local homomorphism (an extension) of Noetherian local rings of mixed characteristic (0, p), with B′ regular and the residue field extension separable. Then B is Cohen–Macaulay.
hypotheses: Separability of the residue extension is André's hypothesis; Heitmann–Ma remove it, which is not a target here.
proofSteps: Pass to completions and perfect residue fields; purity is preserved (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.6/pure-local-completion), B′ stays regular, and Cohen–Macaulayness descends from the faithfully flat extension (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/flat-local-cm).
B is a domain as a pure subring of the domain B′, and β is injective.
DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.6/weak-functoriality-regular-target gives a square of balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras over β.
DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.6/cm-descent-from-regular-target concludes.
acceptance: Invariant rings: if a finite group G acts on a regular local ring B′ of mixed characteristic with |G| invertible in B′, B = B′^G is a pure (Reynolds-split) subring and the theorem makes it Cohen–Macaulay (when the residue extension is separable).
Equal-characteristic analogues are Hochster–Roberts and Boutot; they are not targets of this roadmap.

nodes.title: Derived splinters
nodes.statement: A Noetherian ring A is a derived splinter if for every proper surjective morphism of schemes f : X → Spec A the unit A → RΓ(X, O_X) has a left inverse in the derived category D(A), i.e. its splitting obstruction (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splitting-obstruction) vanishes.
hypotheses: Bhatt's Definition 0.2 [Bhatt12] asks splitting of O_S → Rf_*O_X in D(Coh(S)) for schemes S; for affine S = Spec A this is the definition above, RΓ(X, O_X) being computed by the enhanced pushforward (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/ringed-pullback-pushforward).
Every finite injective ring map A → B gives a finite surjective Spec B → Spec A (lying over), with RΓ = B; so a reduced derived splinter is a splinter.
proofSteps: RΓ(X, O_X) is the derived pushforward of O_X along X → Spec A (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/ringed-pullback-pushforward), an object of D(A) with H^i = H^i(X, O_X) (Tau Ceti Scheme.Modules.Cohomology).
Composition: if A → RΓ(Y, O_Y) splits for some Y → X → Spec A with Y → X proper surjective, then A → RΓ(X, O_X) splits, since the unit for Y factors through the one for X.
acceptance: In characteristic 0 a variety is a derived splinter iff it has rational singularities (Kovács, as recalled in [Bhatt12] Example 1.2); in characteristic p derived splinters are exactly the splinters ([Bhatt12] Theorem 0.3).

sources.match: Defines a derived splinter by splitting of O_S → Rf_*O_X in the derived category of coherent sheaves for every proper surjective f, and shows that over 𝔽_p derived splinters are the splinters.
The derived direct summand theorem: regular Noetherian rings are derived splinters in this sense.

nodes.title: Coherent cohomology of proper schemes over regular rings is perfect
nodes.statement: Let A_0 be a Noetherian ring and f : X → Spec A_0 proper. Then RΓ(X, O_X) is a bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology modules, hence pseudo-coherent (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7/pseudo-coherent-object), and so is the cone of A_0 → RΓ(X, O_X). If A_0 is a regular local ring, these complexes are perfect. For flat A_0 → A_0′, RΓ(X, O_X) ⊗^L_{A_0} A_0′ ≅ RΓ(X ×_{A_0} A_0′, O).
hypotheses: Bhatt uses these facts implicitly in the proof of Theorem 6.1; they are stated here because the localisation of the derived obstruction and its flat base change need them.
proofSteps: Import coherent proper pushforward and R^i f_* from the current StableReduction Layer 2; no extension of that roadmap is requested. Since X is separated and quasi-compact, choose a finite affine cover of t opens. Their intersections are affine and the alternating Čech complex computes quasi-coherent cohomology, so H^i(X,O_X)=0 for i≥t (Stacks Lemma 30.4.2). This finite-cover bound does not require finite Krull dimension of the Noetherian base.
Bounded with finitely generated cohomology over Noetherian A_0 means pseudo-coherent (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7/pseudo-coherent-object).

Over a regular local ring every finitely generated module has finite projective dimension (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3/regular-local-finite-pd), so a pseudo-coherent complex with bounded cohomology is perfect (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7/perfect-complexes-tor-amplitude-and-minimal-models).
Flat base change for quasi-coherent cohomology (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/tor-independent-base-change).
acceptance: For X = Spec B with B finite over A_0, RΓ(X, O_X) = B; over a regular local ring B has finite projective dimension, consistent with perfectness.

sources.match: Assumes A_0 regular local and repeats the argument of Theorem 5.4 for the cone of A_0 → RΓ(X_0, O_{X_0}); the localisation needs a pseudo-coherent cone and the flat base change of its Hom along A_0 → A_∞ needs a perfect cone.
Outlines the derived theorem as the same argument applied to RΓ of a proper map.

A finite affine cover of a quasi-compact scheme with affine diagonal bounds quasi-coherent cohomology; proper coherent pushforward over a locally Noetherian base has finite cohomology over an affine base.

nodes.title: Reductions of the derived splitting problem
nodes.statement: Let A_0 be a Noetherian regular ring and f_0 : X_0 → Spec A_0 proper surjective, with splitting obstruction α ∈ Hom_{D(A_0)}(Q, A_0[1]) of A_0 → RΓ(X_0, O_{X_0}) (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/splitting-obstruction). Then α = 0 iff its image vanishes over the completion of the localisation at every maximal ideal; each such completion is a complete regular local ring of equal characteristic 0, of equal characteristic p, or of mixed characteristic (0, p), and the base-changed map is again proper surjective. Over a complete regular local A_0 one may moreover replace X_0 by an integral closed subscheme Z, proper, surjective and generically finite over A_0; in mixed characteristic there is then g ∈ A_0 nonzero in A_0/p with Z → Spec A_0 finite étale over A_0[1/(pg)].
hypotheses: The pseudo-coherence of Q makes Hom_{D(A_0)}(Q, A_0[1]) commute with flat base change (Stacks 0A6A), so the passage to completed local rings is lossless (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E16, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E15).
proofSteps: Q is pseudo-coherent (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/proper-cohomology-perfect), so for flat A_0 → A_0′, Hom(Q, A_0[1]) ⊗ A_0′ ≅ Hom(Q ⊗^L A_0′, A_0′[1]), and Q ⊗^L A_0′ is the cone for X_0 ×_{A_0} A_0′ by flat base change. A finitely generated module vanishing at every completed local ring vanishes.

Multisection: choose a closed point of the generic fibre of X_0 → Spec A_0 (A_0 a domain) and let Z be its closure, integral, proper, surjective and generically finite; the unit for Z factors through the unit for X_0, so splitting for Z implies splitting for X_0.

Discriminant: Z → Spec A_0 is generically finite étale in characteristic 0, and as in DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions g can be chosen outside the minimal primes of pA_0.
acceptance: For X_0 = Spec B_0 with B_0 finite this reduces to DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/direct-summand-reductions.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1, first sentences, p. 11
sources.match: We may assume A_0 regular local; by taking the closure of a suitable generically defined multisection, X_0 integral and f_0 generically finite; choose g coprime to p with f_0 finite étale after inverting pg.

nodes.title: Proper maps over integral perfectoid algebras are almost split
nodes.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0, A an integral perfectoid K°-algebra and f : Y → Spec A a proper morphism such that f[1/p] is finite étale and surjective. Then A → RΓ(Y, O_Y) has a left inverse in the almost derived category with respect to p^{1/p^∞}.
hypotheses: Surjectivity of f[1/p] is added to Bhatt's Proposition 6.2, which only asks f[1/p] finite étale: if the generic fibre is empty (Y lying over p = 0), the statement fails (source issue DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay/E17, after PAPER-BHATT-18/E1). In the application f[1/p] is surjective because f_0 is.

A may be non-Noetherian and Spf A need not be an admissible locally finite-type formal scheme. AdicSpacesPartII R2’s formal-model theorems therefore do not supply this factorisation; use the scheme blow-up charts directly. Integrality of H⁰(Y,O_Y) over A is used here without claiming finite generation over A.
proofSteps: B = H⁰(Y, O_Y) is integral over A and finite étale after inverting p; almost purity (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem, PerfectoidSpaces:P3/integral-closure-almost-finite-etale) gives B → C, an isomorphism after inverting p, with A → C almost finite étale, faithful by surjectivity, hence almost split (trace, PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-dual-and-trace).

After almost purity replace A by the integral perfectoid closure C of the generic finite étale algebra, and Y by Y ×_{Spec B} Spec C; this reduces to the generic-isomorphism case, and the almost finite étale faithful trace supplies descent of the eventual retraction. Dominate Y by a scheme blow-up of Spec A in a finitely generated ideal containing p^N, using SF.4/modification-domination over a quasi-compact quasi-separated arbitrary base.

Write the blow-up ideal (f_0,…,f_r). The rational domains |f_j|≤|f_i|, with some f_i nonzero since p^N lies in the ideal, cover Spa(A[1/p],A). On each, the bounded fractions f_j/f_i give a map to the corresponding scheme blow-up chart; these glue to a morphism of ringed spaces (Spa(A[1/p],A),O⁺) → Y. This is Bhatt’s footnote 8 argument. No locally finite-type formal model or general Raynaud equivalence is used.
The composite is an almost isomorphism by Scholze's almost vanishing of H^i(S_η, O⁺) for i > 0 (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity), so the first map is almost split.
acceptance: For Y = Spec B finite over A this is the almost splitting of an almost finite étale cover, as in DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/annular-almost-splitting.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.2 and proof, with footnote 8, p. 11
sources.match: Proposition 6.2 gives almost splitting over an integral perfectoid base; add generic surjectivity as in E17. Footnote 8 constructs the factorisation through a scheme blow-up using bounded rational functions, without an admissible finite-type formal model.

nodes.title: Killing higher coherent cohomology by finite covers in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a proper morphism of Noetherian 𝔽_p-schemes. There exist a proper morphism g : Y → S and a finite surjective morphism π : Y → X such that π* : τ^{≥1}Rf_*O_X → τ^{≥1}Rg_*O_Y is zero.
hypotheses: The source is Bhatt [Bhatt12] Theorem 0.4, whose proof follows the method of Hochster–Huneke and Huneke–Lyubeznik (equational lemma and Frobenius); it is cited here as a key theorem with that outline.
proofSteps: Over an affine Noetherian base, each positive coherent cohomology module is finite and Frobenius-stable. For finitely many generators, monic additive Frobenius equations allow finite integral extensions killing the classes (Bhatt 2012 Proposition 3.2 and Corollary 3.5, pp. 7–9). The equational lemma supplies the method; ordinary affine cohomology is not local cohomology.

Choose a finite affine cover of X. Its base changes remain affine, giving a fixed finite Čech bound for the higher cohomology at every later finite cover. Killing all cohomology maps is insufficient by itself to kill a derived morphism: iterate the covers through that finite amplitude, using Bhatt Lemma 2.2, pp. 5–6, to make τ^{≥1}Rf_* → τ^{≥1}Rg_* zero.

For a general Noetherian S choose finitely many affine opens; Proposition 3.1, pp. 6–7, extends and dominates the local finite covers to obtain a common finite surjective cover. The same bounded-complex argument yields the global zero morphism. No induction on potentially infinite Krull dimension is used.
acceptance: For an elliptic curve E over a field of characteristic p, the finite surjective map [p]:E → E acts as multiplication by p on H¹(E,O_E), hence as zero. Since τ^{≥1}RΓ(E,O_E) has only H¹, its induced map is zero. In contrast, X=Spec R already has zero positive ordinary coherent cohomology and cannot test local-cohomology killing.

sources.locator: Theorem 0.4, p. 1; Lemma 2.2 and Propositions 3.1–3.2 with Corollary 3.5, pp. 5–9
sources.match: For f : X → S proper between Noetherian 𝔽_p-schemes there are a proper g : Y → S and a finite surjective π : Y → X with π* zero on τ^{≥1}Rf_*O_X; the proof is inspired by Hochster–Huneke and Huneke–Lyubeznik.

nodes.title: Splinters are derived splinters in characteristic p
nodes.statement: A Noetherian 𝔽_p-algebra is a splinter if and only if it is a derived splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-splinter). In particular every Noetherian regular 𝔽_p-algebra is a derived splinter.
hypotheses: The 'in particular' combines this with DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.1/frobenius-direct-summand, as Bhatt cites [Bhatt12] Theorem 1.4 and Example 2.3 for the characteristic-p case of Theorem 1.2.
proofSteps: Derived splinter ⇒ splinter: finite surjective maps are proper surjective (API isSplinter of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-splinter).

Given X → Spec A proper surjective, choose Y → X finite surjective killing the map on τ^{≥1}. The composite RΓ(X,O_X) → RΓ(Y,O_Y) → τ^{≥1}RΓ(Y,O_Y) is zero. Exactness of Hom applied to the truncation triangle H⁰(Y,O_Y) → RΓ(Y,O_Y) → τ^{≥1}RΓ(Y,O_Y) therefore lifts the first map to RΓ(X,O_X) → H⁰(Y,O_Y).

The lift preserves the unit: Hom(A,H⁰(Y,O_Y)) → Hom(A,RΓ(Y,O_Y)) is an isomorphism by the standard t-structure. The finite algebra H⁰(Y,O_Y) has surjective spectrum over A by proper surjectivity of Y → Spec A; since a splinter is reduced, its structure map is injective. Its A-linear splitting composed with the lift retracts A → RΓ(X,O_X).
acceptance: 𝔽_p⟦x, y⟧ is a derived splinter, by DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.1/frobenius-direct-summand and this theorem.

sources.locator: Theorem 0.3, p. 1, proof p. 9; Example 1.3, pp. 2–3
sources.match: A Noetherian 𝔽_p-scheme is a splinter iff it is a derived splinter; regular affine 𝔽_p-schemes are splinters.
The characteristic p case of Theorem 1.2 follows from [Bhatt12] Theorem 1.4 and Example 2.3.

nodes.title: The derived direct summand theorem for regular rings containing ℚ
nodes.statement: Every Noetherian regular ring containing ℚ is a derived splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-splinter).
hypotheses: Kovács Theorem 1, p. 187, is descent of rational singularities assuming the source already has rational singularities. Theorem 2, p. 188, gives splitting for a surjective morphism of projective complex varieties when both varieties have rational singularities. Neither theorem by itself states the arbitrary proper, arbitrary characteristic-zero-base assertion needed here.
Kovács' theorem rests on resolution of singularities in characteristic 0 and on Grauert–Riemenschneider vanishing, which no roadmap of the atlas plans: gap G2.
proofSteps: Reduce to A_0 a complete regular local ring containing ℚ (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-obstruction-reductions); the obstruction lies in Ext¹ of a bounded coherent complex and commutes with the faithfully flat completion.

Use Popescu approximation and finite-presentation limits to seek a smooth finite-type stage carrying the proper cover and its obstruction; descent of surjectivity and compatibility of the retraction require explicit limit arguments, retained in G2 rather than inferred solely from the algebra colimit.

For complex varieties the derived-splinter/rational-singularity characterisation is recalled in Bhatt 2012 Example 1.2, p. 2. To derive it in the needed generality from Kovács Theorems 1–2 requires resolution and Grauert–Riemenschneider vanishing, plus reduction from arbitrary proper covers to the projective rational-source situation. Extension to general characteristic-zero fields, localisation, and the approximation step are all included in G2.
acceptance: For A_0 = K a field of characteristic 0 the statement is the degenerate case of DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-splinter.
The finite (underived) case is the trace argument DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.0/trace-retraction; the elliptic cone shows the derived statement is genuinely stronger.

sources.match: When A_0 has characteristic 0 the theorem is due to Kovács and follows from Spec A_0 having rational singularities.
A complex variety is a derived splinter iff it has rational singularities, referring to Kovács for the proof.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p. 187; Theorem 2 and proof, pp. 188–191
sources.match: Theorem 1 descends rational singularities along a morphism with a derived retraction when the source has rational singularities. Theorem 2 supplies a derived retraction for a surjective map of projective complex varieties with rational singularities on both sides. The extension needed for the roadmap is G2, not the literal statement of either theorem.

nodes.title: The derived direct summand theorem
nodes.statement: Let A_0 be a Noetherian regular ring and f_0 : X_0 → Spec A_0 a proper surjective morphism. Then A_0 → RΓ(X_0, O_{X_0}) has a left inverse in D(A_0); that is, every Noetherian regular ring is a derived splinter (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-splinter).
hypotheses: In mixed characteristic the theorem was new even in dimension 2 when Bhatt proved it; it implies the direct summand theorem for reduced finite covers and is orthogonal to it for birational f_0 (blow-ups).
proofSteps: Reduce to A_0 complete regular local of one of the three characteristic types, and to Z integral, generically finite, finite étale over A_0[1/(pg)] (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/derived-obstruction-reductions).
Equal characteristic 0: DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/char-zero-derived-splitting. Equal characteristic p: DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/char-p-derived-splinter.

Mixed characteristic: the cone Q_0 is perfect (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/proper-cohomology-perfect). If α_0 ≠ 0, DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/obstruction-detection gives m, k with (pg)^{1/p^k} ∉ Ann(α_∞/p^m).

For fixed m, n the base change of Z to A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩ is proper and finite étale and surjective after inverting p (g divides p^n), so A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m → RΓ(Z, O) ⊗^L A_∞⟨p^n/g⟩/p^m is almost split (DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.7/perfectoid-proper-almost-split).
DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.3/obstruction-limit makes α_∞/p^m almost zero for (pg)^{1/p^∞}, a contradiction; hence α_0 = 0.
acceptance: For f_0 finite and A_0 → B_0 injective the theorem is the direct summand theorem DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay:DS.5/direct-summand-theorem.

For f_0 the blow-up of a regular local ring of dimension d at its maximal ideal, RΓ(X_0, O) = A_0 and the splitting is trivial; for alterations of regular schemes it says coherent cohomology loses nothing.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 6.1 with proof, pp. 1 and 11
sources.match: For a regular Noetherian A_0 and proper surjective f_0, A_0 → RΓ(X_0, O) splits in D(A_0); the mixed characteristic proof repeats that of Theorem 5.4 with Proposition 6.2 replacing almost purity on the annuli.
The derived theorem has geometric consequences inaccessible from the finite one, and its proof follows the same outline.

gaps.detail: Kovács’ author copy was independently read in full (pp. 187–191). Theorem 1 assumes the source has rational singularities; Theorem 2 is for surjective morphisms of projective complex varieties with rational singularities on both sides. gaps.title: G4: finite bad witnesses for pointed partial modifications
gaps.detail: Prove that a finite bad witness in full algebra modifications, including the two-base double-sequence version, can be realised by a finite sequence of the explicitly pointed scalar-polynomial module quotients in DS.4/partial-algebra-modification. Conversely extend pointed maps into a big Cohen–Macaulay algebra by evaluation. Hochster Theorem 4.2 pp. 8–9 and Heitmann–Ma Theorem 1.6 pp. 3–4 state the intended criterion, but their module formula suppresses a distinguished coefficient and Hochster’s asserted fixed-relation N-colimit is false (E21–E22). A precise finite-witness construction, or a replacement module construction with a proved comparison, is required before this interface can be implemented as the cited criterion. No new algebra structure is inferred from a module colimit.
